requirements.statement: Under 15.001, a proposal modification is a change before the solicitation closing date and time, a change responding to an amendment, or a change correcting a mistake before award. The supplied item_kind is a case fact, not a classification to infer.
requirements.quote: Proposal modification is a change made to a proposal before the solicitation closing date and time, or made in response to an amendment, or made to correct a mistake at any time before award.

requirements.statement: Under 15.001, a proposal revision is a post-closing change requested or allowed by the contracting officer as a result of negotiations.
requirements.quote: Proposal revision is a change to a proposal made after the solicitation closing date, at the request of or as allowed by a contracting officer, as the result of negotiations.

requirements.statement: Submit proposals, revisions, and modifications so they reach the designated Government office by the specified solicitation time.
requirements.quote: Offerors are responsible for submitting proposals, and any revisions, and modifications, so as to reach the Government office designated in the solicitation by the time specified in the solicitation.

requirements.statement: Use any transmission method authorized by the solicitation.
requirements.quote: Offerors may use any transmission method authorized by the solicitation (i.e., regular mail, electronic commerce, or facsimile).

requirements.statement: If the solicitation specifies no receipt time, the receipt time is 4:30 p.m. local time at the designated Government office on the due date. This is a deadline-establishment rule, not an additional condition to infer from the supplied inputs.
requirements.quote: If no time is specified in the solicitation, the time for receipt is 4:30 p.m., local time, for the designated Government office on the date that proposals are due.

requirements.statement: Mark submissions with their receipt date and time upon receipt at the specified location.
requirements.quote: Upon receipt at the location specified in the solicitation, proposals and information received in response to a request for information (RFI) shall be marked with the date and time of receipt and shall be transmitted to the designated officials.

requirements.statement: Transmit received submissions to the designated officials.
requirements.quote: Upon receipt at the location specified in the solicitation, proposals and information received in response to a request for information (RFI) shall be marked with the date and time of receipt and shall be transmitted to the designated officials.

requirements.statement: Safeguard proposals against unauthorized disclosure throughout source selection.
requirements.quote: Proposals shall be safeguarded from unauthorized disclosure throughout the source selection process.

requirements.statement: If an electronically transmitted or facsimile proposal is partly unreadable, immediately notify the offeror and permit resubmission of the unreadable portion.
requirements.quote: If any portion of a proposal received by the contracting officer electronically or by facsimile is unreadable, the contracting officer immediately shall notify the offeror and permit the offeror to resubmit the unreadable portion of the proposal.

requirements.statement: After consulting the offeror, prescribe the method and time for resubmission of an unreadable portion and document them in the file.
requirements.quote: The method and time for resubmission shall be prescribed by the contracting officer after consultation with the offeror, and documented in the file.

requirements.statement: For timeliness under 15.208(a), treat an unreadable-portion resubmission as received at the original submission's receipt date and time if the offeror complies with the prescribed resubmission time and format. No corresponding case facts are supplied for a separate automated determination.
requirements.quote: The resubmission shall be considered as if it were received at the date and time of the original unreadable submission for the purpose of determining timeliness under 15.208(a), provided the offeror complies with the time and format requirements for resubmission prescribed by the contracting officer.

requirements.statement: A proposal, modification, or revision received at the designated Government office after the exact specified receipt time is late. For the decision interface, received_late supplies that determination using the effective deadline.
requirements.quote: Any proposal, modification, or revision, that is received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is "late"

requirements.statement: Do not consider a late proposal, modification, or revision unless the general exception in 15.208(b)(1) or the overriding successful-proposal modification rule in 15.208(b)(2) applies.
requirements.quote: Any proposal, modification, or revision, that is received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is "late" and will not be considered unless it is received before award is made, the contracting officer determines that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition; and-

requirements.statement: The general 15.208(b)(1) exception requires receipt before award; this prerequisite does not limit the separate 15.208(b)(2) rule.
requirements.quote: will not be considered unless it is received before award is made

requirements.statement: The general 15.208(b)(1) exception also requires the contracting officer's determination that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition.
requirements.quote: the contracting officer determines that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition

requirements.statement: One alternative under the general exception is transmission by a solicitation-authorized electronic commerce method and receipt at the initial Government infrastructure entry point no later than 5:00 p.m. one working day before the proposal due date. Earlier working days qualify regardless of their minute of receipt.
requirements.quote: If it was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the solicitation, it was received at the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure not later than 5:00 p.m. one working day prior to the date specified for receipt of proposals; or

requirements.statement: Another alternative requires acceptable evidence establishing both receipt at the designated Government installation and Government control before the receipt deadline. All three supplied facts must hold for this route.
requirements.quote: There is acceptable evidence to establish that it was received at the Government installation designated for receipt of proposals and was under the Government’s control prior to the time set for receipt of proposals; or

requirements.statement: Being the only proposal received is the third alternative under the general exception. It remains subject to the preaward-receipt and no-undue-delay prerequisites.
requirements.quote: It was the only proposal received.

requirements.statement: Consider a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal that makes its terms more favorable to the Government at any time it is received. This special rule takes precedence over the general late-item prerequisites.
requirements.quote: However, a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted.

requirements.statement: A qualifying late modification under 15.208(b)(2) may be accepted. The considerable output does not decide acceptance or award.
requirements.quote: However, a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted.

requirements.statement: Acceptable installation-receipt evidence includes an installation time/date stamp on the wrapper, other installation-maintained documentary receipt evidence, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel. The source list is inclusive, not an exclusive evidence checklist.
requirements.quote: Acceptable evidence to establish the time of receipt at the Government installation includes the time/date stamp of that installation on the proposal wrapper, other documentary evidence of receipt maintained by the installation, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.

requirements.statement: The deemed deadline extension triggers when an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes, that interruption prevents timely receipt at the designated office, and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the closing date.
requirements.quote: If an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes so that proposals cannot be received at the Government office designated for receipt of proposals by the exact time specified in the solicitation, and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the solicitation closing date

requirements.statement: When the emergency rule triggers, the extended deadline is the same specified time of day on the first workday normal Government processes resume. Do not invent a calendar date from the supplied facts.
requirements.quote: the time specified for receipt of proposals will be deemed to be extended to the same time of day specified in the solicitation on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume.

requirements.statement: Promptly notify the offeror that its proposal, modification, or revision was received late, unless both parts of the notice exception apply.
requirements.quote: The contracting officer must promptly notify any offeror if its proposal, modification, or revision was received late, and must inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered, unless contract award is imminent and the notice prescribed in 15.503(b) would suffice.

requirements.statement: In the required late-receipt notification, inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered.
requirements.quote: must inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered, unless contract award is imminent and the notice prescribed in 15.503(b) would suffice.

requirements.statement: The 15.208(f) notice exception requires both imminent contract award and sufficiency of the notice prescribed in 15.503(b). Neither fact alone removes this notice duty. Sufficiency is supplied externally rather than inferred.
requirements.quote: unless contract award is imminent and the notice prescribed in 15.503(b) would suffice.

requirements.statement: Hold late proposals and modifications that are not considered unopened until after award, except that opening for identification is allowed. Do not extend this particular requirement to revisions merely by analogy.
requirements.quote: Late proposals and modifications that are not considered must be held unopened, unless opened for identification, until after award and then retained with other unsuccessful proposals.

requirements.statement: After award, retain unconsidered late proposals and modifications with the other unsuccessful proposals.
requirements.quote: Late proposals and modifications that are not considered must be held unopened, unless opened for identification, until after award and then retained with other unsuccessful proposals.

requirements.statement: For each scoped late proposal, modification, or revision, include the date and hour of receipt in the contracting office files if available.
requirements.quote: If available, the following must be included in the contracting office files for each late proposal, modification, revision, or withdrawal: (1) The date and hour of receipt.

requirements.statement: For each scoped late proposal, modification, or revision, include a statement whether the proposal was considered for award and its supporting rationale in the files if available. Do not substitute an award determination for the bounded consideration output.
requirements.quote: If available, the following must be included in the contracting office files for each late proposal, modification, revision, or withdrawal: (1) The date and hour of receipt. (2) A statement regarding whether the proposal was considered for award, with supporting rationale.

requirements.statement: For each scoped late proposal, modification, or revision, include the envelope, wrapper, or other evidence of receipt date in the files if available.
requirements.quote: If available, the following must be included in the contracting office files for each late proposal, modification, revision, or withdrawal: (1) The date and hour of receipt. (2) A statement regarding whether the proposal was considered for award, with supporting rationale. (3) The envelope, wrapper, or other evidence of date of receipt.

process.action: Establish scope and provenance. This is an unapproved model draft interpreting only the supplied FAR Part 15 edition, FAC 2026-01, effective 2026-03-13. The automated outputs are bounded to 15.208(b), (f), and (d); related receipt, evidence, and recordkeeping actions support that scoped process. Withdrawal decisions and unrelated procurement procedures are outside this interface. Dependency edges and first-match evaluation are implementation choices, not additional source obligations.
process.quote: This part prescribes policies and procedures governing competitive and noncompetitive negotiated acquisitions.

process.action: Identify the submitted item using the supplied item_kind. Preserve the distinction between a modification and a revision; do not reclassify the supplied case fact or apply the special modification rule to a revision.
process.quote: Proposal modification is a change made to a proposal before the solicitation closing date and time, or made in response to an amendment, or made to correct a mistake at any time before award. Proposal revision is a change to a proposal made after the solicitation closing date, at the request of or as allowed by a contracting officer, as the result of negotiations.

process.action: Evaluate emergency_deadline_extension independently of whether the submitted item is late. Require all three supplied interruption, prevention, and urgency facts. If triggered, preserve the new deadline as the same specified time of day on the first workday normal Government processes resume; no resumption date is supplied. The received_late input already incorporates any applicable emergency extension and must not be recalculated or automatically set false.
process.quote: If an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes so that proposals cannot be received at the Government office designated for receipt of proposals by the exact time specified in the solicitation, and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the solicitation closing date, the time specified for receipt of proposals will be deemed to be extended to the same time of day specified in the solicitation on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume.

process.action: Preserve the specified receipt deadline and authorized transmission methods. If establishing a deadline outside the supplied case facts and no time is specified, use 4:30 p.m. local time at the designated office on the due date. Do not confuse that receipt deadline with the separate 5:00 p.m. electronic-gateway exception cutoff.
process.quote: Offerors are responsible for submitting proposals, and any revisions, and modifications, so as to reach the Government office designated in the solicitation by the time specified in the solicitation. Offerors may use any transmission method authorized by the solicitation (i.e., regular mail, electronic commerce, or facsimile). If no time is specified in the solicitation, the time for receipt is 4:30 p.m., local time, for the designated Government office on the date that proposals are due.

process.action: Upon receipt at the specified location, mark the submission's receipt date and time and transmit it to designated officials. Safeguard the proposal against unauthorized disclosure.
process.quote: Upon receipt at the location specified in the solicitation, proposals and information received in response to a request for information (RFI) shall be marked with the date and time of receipt and shall be transmitted to the designated officials. (b) Proposals shall be safeguarded from unauthorized disclosure throughout the source selection process.

process.action: When an electronic or facsimile proposal has an unreadable portion, immediately notify the offeror, permit resubmission, and prescribe and document the method and time after consultation. A compliant resubmission retains the original unreadable submission's receipt time for 15.208(a). This is a conditional manual handling step: the interface supplies no unreadability or compliance fields, so do not invent those facts or override received_late.
process.quote: If any portion of a proposal received by the contracting officer electronically or by facsimile is unreadable, the contracting officer immediately shall notify the offeror and permit the offeror to resubmit the unreadable portion of the proposal. The method and time for resubmission shall be prescribed by the contracting officer after consultation with the offeror, and documented in the file. The resubmission shall be considered as if it were received at the date and time of the original unreadable submission for the purpose of determining timeliness under 15.208(a), provided the offeror complies with the time and format requirements for resubmission prescribed by the contracting officer.

process.action: Use received_late as supplied. If false, return unknown for late_submission_considerable because that output concerns late-item exceptions, not ordinary consideration. If true, proceed through the special and general late-item routes. Retain the independent emergency result.
process.quote: Any proposal, modification, or revision, that is received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is "late"

process.action: For a late item, evaluate the successful-proposal modification rule before the general exception. If item_kind is modification, otherwise_successful_proposal is true, and modified_terms_more_favourable is true, return true for late_submission_considerable regardless of preaward receipt, undue delay, or the general receipt routes. Consideration is mandatory under this rule, but acceptance is only permitted and is not an output.
process.quote: However, a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted.

process.action: For the general installation-receipt route, use acceptable_receipt_evidence as supplied and preserve both required historical facts: receipt at the designated installation and Government control before the deadline. Evidence may include an installation stamp, other installation-maintained documents, or Government personnel testimony or statements; do not impose an exclusive documentary-evidence requirement.
process.quote: Acceptable evidence to establish the time of receipt at the Government installation includes the time/date stamp of that installation on the proposal wrapper, other documentary evidence of receipt maintained by the installation, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.

process.action: If no special-rule match applies to a late item, require receipt before award and no undue acquisition delay, together with at least one alternative: authorized electronic submission meeting the initial-gateway cutoff; acceptable evidence of timely designated-installation receipt and Government control; or only_proposal_received. Implement the gateway cutoff as a working-day distance greater than 1, or a distance equal to 1 with minute of day at most 1020. Return false if the late item satisfies neither the special nor the general exception. This false result addresses only consideration under 15.208(b), not award or general lawfulness.
process.quote: Any proposal, modification, or revision, that is received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is "late" and will not be considered unless it is received before award is made, the contracting officer determines that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition; and- (i) If it was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the solicitation, it was received at the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure not later than 5:00 p.m. one working day prior to the date specified for receipt of proposals; or (ii) There is acceptable evidence to establish that it was received at the Government installation designated for receipt of proposals and was under the Government’s control prior to the time set for receipt of proposals; or (iii) It was the only proposal received.

process.action: Determine late_notice_required separately from eligibility for consideration. For every late proposal, modification, or revision, promptly notify the offeror of late receipt and whether the proposal will be considered unless contract_award_imminent and award_notice_would_suffice are both true. Do not add a preaward-receipt restriction or excuse notice merely because the item will be considered. Treat sufficiency of the 15.503(b) notice as the supplied external procedural fact; this output does not decide other notice duties.
process.quote: The contracting officer must promptly notify any offeror if its proposal, modification, or revision was received late, and must inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered, unless contract award is imminent and the notice prescribed in 15.503(b) would suffice.

process.action: For an unconsidered late proposal or modification, hold it unopened until after award, except for opening needed for identification; after award retain it with other unsuccessful proposals. Do not infer that 15.208(g) imposes this same disposition duty on revisions. This handling step does not authorize delaying the prompt notice.
process.quote: Late proposals and modifications that are not considered must be held unopened, unless opened for identification, until after award and then retained with other unsuccessful proposals.

process.action: For each scoped late item, include available receipt date and hour, the statement whether the proposal was considered for award with supporting rationale, and the envelope, wrapper, or other receipt-date evidence in the contracting office files. Record the applicable special or general exception and any notice exception without inventing missing evidence. Recordkeeping is ongoing; this dependency does not postpone promptly required notification or initial preservation.
process.quote: If available, the following must be included in the contracting office files for each late proposal, modification, revision, or withdrawal: (1) The date and hour of receipt. (2) A statement regarding whether the proposal was considered for award, with supporting rationale. (3) The envelope, wrapper, or other evidence of date of receipt.

requirements.statement: Offerors must submit proposals, revisions and modifications so that they reach the Government office designated in the solicitation by the time the solicitation specifies.
requirements.quote: Offerors are responsible for submitting proposals, and any revisions, and modifications, so as to reach the Government office designated in the solicitation by the time specified in the solicitation.

requirements.statement: Offerors may use any transmission method the solicitation authorises, such as regular mail, electronic commerce or facsimile.
requirements.quote: Offerors may use any transmission method authorized by the solicitation (i.e., regular mail, electronic commerce, or facsimile).

requirements.statement: If the solicitation specifies no time, the time for receipt is 4:30 p.m. local time at the designated Government office on the proposal due date.
requirements.quote: If no time is specified in the solicitation, the time for receipt is 4:30 p.m., local time, for the designated Government office on the date that proposals are due.

requirements.statement: A proposal, modification or revision received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is late.
requirements.quote: Any proposal, modification, or revision, that is received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is

requirements.statement: Under 15.208(b)(1), a late item will not be considered unless all of the following are true: (a) it is received before award; (b) the contracting officer determines that accepting it would not unduly delay the acquisition; and (c) one of the exceptions in (b)(1)(i) through (iii) applies.
requirements.quote: will not be considered unless it is received before award is made, the contracting officer determines that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition

requirements.statement: Exception (b)(1)(i): the item was sent through an electronic commerce method the solicitation authorises, and it reached the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure no later than 5:00 p.m. one working day before the date specified for receipt.
requirements.quote: If it was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the solicitation, it was received at the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure not later than 5:00 p.m. one working day prior to the date specified for receipt of proposals

requirements.statement: Exception (b)(1)(ii): acceptable evidence establishes two facts. First, the item was received at the Government installation designated for receipt. Second, it was under the Government's control before the time set for receipt.
requirements.quote: There is acceptable evidence to establish that it was received at the Government installation designated for receipt of proposals and was under the Government’s control prior to the time set for receipt of proposals

requirements.statement: Exception (b)(1)(iii): the item was the only proposal received.
requirements.quote: It was the only proposal received.

requirements.statement: Notwithstanding (b)(1), a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal that makes its terms more favourable to the Government will be considered whenever it is received. This rule takes precedence over the (b)(1) conditions.
requirements.quote: However, a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received

requirements.statement: Such a late, more-favourable modification of an otherwise successful proposal may be accepted. Acceptance is permitted, not required.
requirements.quote: will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted

requirements.statement: Acceptable evidence of the time of receipt at the Government installation includes any of the following: (a) the installation's time/date stamp on the proposal wrapper; (b) other documentary evidence of receipt kept by the installation; or (c) oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.
requirements.quote: Acceptable evidence to establish the time of receipt at the Government installation includes the time/date stamp of that installation on the proposal wrapper, other documentary evidence of receipt maintained by the installation, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.

requirements.statement: The 15.208(d) extension triggers only when both of the following are true: (a) an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes so that proposals cannot be received at the designated office by the exact specified time; and (b) urgent Government requirements preclude amending the solicitation closing date.
requirements.quote: If an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes so that proposals cannot be received at the Government office designated for receipt of proposals by the exact time specified in the solicitation, and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the solicitation closing date

requirements.statement: When the extension triggers, the time for receipt is deemed extended to the same time of day specified in the solicitation, on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume. The source gives no calendar date.
requirements.quote: the time specified for receipt of proposals will be deemed to be extended to the same time of day specified in the solicitation on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume.

requirements.statement: Proposals may be withdrawn by written notice at any time before award.
requirements.quote: Proposals may be withdrawn by written notice at any time before award.

requirements.statement: The contracting officer must document the contract file when oral withdrawals are made.
requirements.quote: The contracting officer must document the contract file when oral withdrawals are made.

requirements.statement: The contracting officer must promptly notify any offeror whose proposal, modification or revision was received late. The notice must say whether the proposal will be considered.
requirements.quote: The contracting officer must promptly notify any offeror if its proposal, modification, or revision was received late, and must inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered

requirements.statement: Exception to the 15.208(f) late-notice duty: the duty does not apply when both (a) contract award is imminent and (b) the 15.503(b) notice would suffice.
requirements.quote: unless contract award is imminent and the notice prescribed in 15.503(b) would suffice.

requirements.statement: Late proposals and modifications that are not considered must be held unopened, unless opened for identification, until after award. They are then retained with the other unsuccessful proposals.
requirements.quote: Late proposals and modifications that are not considered must be held unopened, unless opened for identification, until after award and then retained with other unsuccessful proposals.

requirements.statement: If available, the contracting office files for each late proposal, modification, revision or withdrawal must include the date and hour of receipt.
requirements.quote: If available, the following must be included in the contracting office files for each late proposal, modification, revision, or withdrawal:

requirements.statement: The file must include a statement of whether the proposal was considered for award, with supporting rationale.
requirements.quote: A statement regarding whether the proposal was considered for award, with supporting rationale.

requirements.statement: The file must include the envelope, wrapper or other evidence of the date of receipt.
requirements.quote: The envelope, wrapper, or other evidence of date of receipt.

requirements.statement: A proposal modification is a change to a proposal made in any of three ways: (a) before the solicitation closing date and time; (b) in response to an amendment; or (c) to correct a mistake at any time before award.
requirements.quote: Proposal modification is a change made to a proposal before the solicitation closing date and time, or made in response to an amendment, or made to correct a mistake at any time before award.

requirements.statement: A proposal revision is a change to a proposal made after the solicitation closing date, as the result of negotiations, at the request of or as allowed by the contracting officer.
requirements.quote: Proposal revision is a change to a proposal made after the solicitation closing date, at the request of or as allowed by a contracting officer, as the result of negotiations.

requirements.statement: On receipt at the location specified in the solicitation, proposals must be marked with the date and time of receipt and transmitted to the designated officials.
requirements.quote: Upon receipt at the location specified in the solicitation, proposals and information received in response to a request for information (RFI) shall be marked with the date and time of receipt and shall be transmitted to the designated officials.

requirements.statement: When electronic commerce is used to receive proposals, modifications and revisions, the RFP must specify the electronic commerce methods offerors may use.
requirements.quote: Electronic commerce may be used to issue RFPs and to receive proposals, modifications, and revisions. In this case, the RFP shall specify the electronic commerce method(s) that offerors may use (see subpart 4.5).

requirements.statement: Contracting officers may authorise receipt of proposals, modifications or revisions by facsimile.
requirements.quote: Contracting officers may issue RFPs and/or authorize receipt of proposals, modifications, or revisions by facsimile.

requirements.statement: If any portion of a proposal received electronically or by facsimile is unreadable, the contracting officer must immediately notify the offeror and permit resubmission of that portion.
requirements.quote: If any portion of a proposal received by the contracting officer electronically or by facsimile is unreadable, the contracting officer immediately shall notify the offeror and permit the offeror to resubmit the unreadable portion of the proposal.

requirements.statement: For 15.208(a) timeliness, a compliant resubmission of an unreadable portion is treated as received at the date and time of the original unreadable submission.
requirements.quote: The resubmission shall be considered as if it were received at the date and time of the original unreadable submission for the purpose of determining timeliness under 15.208(a), provided the offeror complies with the time and format requirements for resubmission prescribed by the contracting officer.

requirements.statement: Oral presentations are subject to the same timing restrictions as written information under 15.208.
requirements.quote: are subject to the same restrictions as written information, regarding timing (see 15.208) and content (see 15.306).

requirements.statement: A common cut-off date is required only for receipt of final proposal revisions.
requirements.quote: The contracting officer is required to establish a common cut-off date only for receipt of final proposal revisions.

requirements.statement: Context for the 15.208(f) exception: under 15.503(b)(1), the contracting officer must give written postaward notice within 3 days after award to certain unsuccessful offerors. Whether that notice would suffice is supplied as an input fact.

requirements.statement: The supplied edition applies to FEMA awards made or disasters declared on or after October 1, 2024. This blueprint uses that fixed edition; the supplied inputs do not establish an award or declaration date.
requirements.quote: This document applies to all FEMA awards made or disasters declared on or after October 1, 2024, and includes the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Revisions to the federal procurement standards effective on October 1, 2024.

requirements.statement: The recipient or subrecipient remains responsible for ensuring that its contract language meets the applicable federal procurement requirements.
requirements.quote: The recipient or subrecipient is solely responsible for ensuring that all language included in its contracts meets the requirements of 2 C.F.R. Part 200, including 2 C.F.R. § 200.327 and Appendix II.

requirements.statement: A contract is the instrument used to purchase property or services needed to carry out the federally funded project or program; it is not itself a federal award or subaward.
requirements.quote: A contract, for the purposes of this Guide, does not mean a federal award or subaward.

requirements.statement: The guide does not supply separate state, tribal, or local contract-provision requirements. A false scoped output does not determine obligations under those laws.
requirements.quote: Contract provisions required by applicable state, tribal, or local laws or rules separate from the federal procurement standards.

requirements.statement: When section 2.1 applies, the contract must address termination for both cause and convenience, including the manner of termination and the basis for settlement.
requirements.quote: Contracts must address termination for cause and for convenience by the recipient or subrecipient, including the manner by which it will be carried out and the basis for settlement.

requirements.statement: Section 2.1 requires the termination provision for contracts and purchase orders exceeding $10,000; exactly $10,000 does not exceed the threshold.
requirements.quote: This contract provision is required for contracts and purchase orders exceeding $10,000.

requirements.statement: At or below $10,000, FEMA suggests a termination-for-cause provision but does not require it under section 2.1. This is a recommendation, not a prohibition on including the provision.
requirements.quote: For contracts at or below $10,000, FEMA suggests including a termination for cause provision, but this is not required.

requirements.statement: FEMA recommends actionable and specific termination clauses; this recommendation is distinct from the applicability threshold and required substantive contents.
requirements.quote: FEMA recommends that termination clauses be actionable and specific.

requirements.statement: Section 4.1 requires a Davis-Bacon compliance provision for prime construction contracts over $2,000 when required by federal program legislation, subject to the express PA/HMA exclusion.
requirements.quote: When required by the federal program legislation, all prime construction contracts over $2,000 awarded by recipients or subrecipients must include a provision for compliance with the Davis-Bacon Act.

requirements.statement: The Davis-Bacon clause is not federally required for PA or HMA procurements. This express program exclusion takes precedence over the general construction, amount, and legislation conditions for this scoped decision.
requirements.quote: However, the Davis-Bacon Act clause is not federally required for procurements under FEMA’s Public Assistance (PA) or Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) Programs.

requirements.statement: The guide directs recipients and subrecipients toward program guidance or their FEMA representative to resolve program applicability. The blueprint does not infer an affirmative or negative legislative requirement from an unknown supplied fact.
requirements.quote: Recipients and subrecipients should refer to applicable NOFO or other program guidance or contact their applicable FEMA grant representative to determine if this provision is required for the procurement.

requirements.statement: When Davis-Bacon applies, contractors must pay laborers and mechanics at least the prevailing wages specified in the Secretary of Labor's wage determination.
requirements.quote: This statute requires that contractors must pay wages to laborers and mechanics at a rate not less than the prevailing wages specified in the Secretary of Labor’s wage determination.

requirements.statement: When Davis-Bacon applies, contractors must pay wages at least weekly.
requirements.quote: Additionally, contractors are required to pay wages at least once per week.

requirements.statement: When Davis-Bacon applies, place the Department of Labor's current prevailing wage determination in each solicitation.
requirements.quote: The recipient or subrecipient must place a copy of the Department of Labor’s current prevailing wage determination in each solicitation.

requirements.statement: When Davis-Bacon applies, award contracts and subcontracts on the condition that the prevailing wage determination is accepted.
requirements.quote: Contracts or subcontracts must be awarded on the condition that the prevailing wage determination is accepted.

requirements.statement: When Davis-Bacon applies, report all suspected or reported violations to the federal agency.
requirements.quote: The recipient or subrecipient must report all suspected or reported violations to the federal agency.

requirements.statement: Contracts subject to Davis-Bacon must also provide for Copeland Anti-Kickback Act compliance; its regulatory requirements are incorporated into the required Davis-Bacon provision, so a separate provision is not necessary.
requirements.quote: According to 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(5), the regulatory requirements for the Copeland “Anti-Kickback” Act are incorporated by reference into the required contract provision, so a separate contract provision is not necessary.

requirements.statement: A separate Copeland Anti-Kickback Act provision may be included even though the required Davis-Bacon provision already incorporates the regulatory requirements.
requirements.quote: However, the recipient or subrecipient may include a separate contract provision specific to the Copeland “Anti-Kickback” Act.

requirements.statement: When Davis-Bacon applies, section 4.3 requires the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) in full in applicable contracts.
requirements.quote: If applicable per the standard described above, the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) in full into all applicable contracts, and all applicable contractors must include these provisions in full in any subcontracts.

requirements.statement: Section 4.3 requires applicable contractors to include the Davis-Bacon provisions in full in subcontracts. Section 4.2 also describes inserting or incorporating the clauses by reference; full insertion satisfies both descriptions without relying on incorporation alone.
requirements.quote: If applicable per the standard described above, the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) in full into all applicable contracts, and all applicable contractors must include these provisions in full in any subcontracts.

requirements.statement: Section 6.1 states an over-$100,000 applicability threshold involving mechanics, laborers, and construction work. Prime construction with the supplied employment fact is expressly covered; the source and supplied facts do not necessarily classify other work.
requirements.quote: This required contract provision applies to all procurements over $100,000 that involve the employment of mechanics, laborers, and construction work.

requirements.statement: Open-market supplies, materials, or articles, transportation contracts, and transmission-of-intelligence contracts are excluded from the section 6.1 requirements, even when an amount or employment condition would otherwise be met.
requirements.quote: These requirements do not apply to the purchase of supplies, materials, or articles ordinarily available on the open market, contracts for transportation or transmission of intelligence.

requirements.statement: When section 6 applies, include 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5) verbatim in applicable contracts.
requirements.quote: If applicable per the standard described above, the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5), verbatim, into all applicable contracts, and all applicable contractors must include these provisions, in full, into any subcontracts.

requirements.statement: When section 6 applies, applicable contractors must include the required work-hours provisions in full in subcontracts.
requirements.quote: If applicable per the standard described above, the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5), verbatim, into all applicable contracts, and all applicable contractors must include these provisions, in full, into any subcontracts.

requirements.statement: For a contract subject only to the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act and not to other statutes cited in 29 C.F.R. § 5.1, also insert a clause meeting 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(c). The declared inputs do not establish this separate condition.
requirements.quote: In addition to the required language from 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5), in any contract subject only to the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act and not to any other statutes cited in 29 C.F.R. § 5.1, the recipient or subrecipient must also insert a clause meeting the requirements of 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(c).

requirements.statement: The additional section 5.5(c) clause has substantive requirements but no mandated specific wording in this guide; FEMA's supplied wording is suggested.
requirements.quote: Specific language is not required, but FEMA has provided suggested language below.

requirements.statement: When the work-hours requirements apply, base wages for mechanics and laborers on a standard 40-hour work week.
requirements.quote: Under 40 U.S.C. § 3702, each contractor must base wages for every mechanic and laborer on a standard 40-hour work week.

requirements.statement: Work exceeding 40 hours per work week is allowed if all excess hours are paid at least one and one-half times the base pay rate.
requirements.quote: Work over 40 hours is allowed, so long as the worker is paid at least one and a half times the base pay rate for all hours worked over 40 in the work week.

requirements.statement: For construction work to which the section applies, laborers' and mechanics' work surroundings and conditions must not be unsanitary or unsafe.
requirements.quote: Additionally, for construction work, under 40 U.S.C. § 3704, work surroundings and conditions for laborers and mechanics must not be unsanitary or unsafe.

requirements.statement: Section 8.1 requires the Clean Air/Water provision for all procurements over $150,000. Exactly $150,000 does not satisfy this amount condition.
requirements.quote: This contract provision is required for all procurements over $150,000.

requirements.statement: When section 8.1 applies, the contract must require contractor compliance with both the Clean Air Act and the Federal Water Pollution Control Act.
requirements.quote: Contracts must contain a provision requiring contractors to comply with the Clean Air Act

requirements.statement: Report violations to FEMA and the Regional Office of the Environmental Protection Agency.
requirements.quote: Violations must be reported to FEMA and the Regional Office of the Environmental Protection Agency.

process.action: For cases not resolved by the program exclusion, evaluate the over-$2,000 amount, prime-construction category, and federal-program-legislation requirement. process.action: For nonexcluded categories, return false at or below $100,000 or when mechanics/laborers are not involved. process.action: Evaluate the section 8.1 amount condition independently of category, program, and employment facts. Return true above $150,000 and false at or below $150,000.
process.quote: This contract provision is required for all procurements over $150,000.

process.action: When Davis-Bacon is required, place the current prevailing wage determination in each solicitation and condition award on acceptance of that determination. process.quote: The recipient or subrecipient must place a copy of the Department of Labor’s current prevailing wage determination in each solicitation.

process.action: When Davis-Bacon applies, include section 4.3's provisions in full in applicable contracts and subcontracts. Implementation choice: use full insertion, which satisfies both section 4.3's express in-full instruction and section 4.2's insert-or-incorporate description. Include Copeland compliance through the required provisions; a separate Copeland clause is optional. Arrange the applicable prevailing-wage, weekly-payment, and violation-reporting duties.
process.quote: If applicable per the standard described above, the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) in full into all applicable contracts, and all applicable contractors must include these provisions in full in any subcontracts.

process.action: When section 6 applies, insert 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5) verbatim in applicable contracts and in full in subcontracts. Preserve the required provisions' work-hours, safety, enforcement, flowdown, and anti-retaliation content rather than replacing it with a summary. Unknown applicability calls for review, not an assumed exemption or requirement.
process.quote: If applicable per the standard described above, the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5), verbatim, into all applicable contracts, and all applicable contractors must include these provisions, in full, into any subcontracts.

process.action: For an applicable work-hours contract, separately determine whether it is subject only to that Act and not to any other statutes cited in 29 C.F.R. § 5.1. If that condition is established, add a clause meeting section 5.5(c); FEMA's sample wording is not mandatory. process.quote: In addition to the required language from 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5), in any contract subject only to the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act and not to any other statutes cited in 29 C.F.R. § 5.1, the recipient or subrecipient must also insert a clause meeting the requirements of 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(c).

process.action: When the section 8.1 amount condition is met, include compliance provisions for both environmental statutes and arrange reporting to FEMA and the EPA Regional Office. Treat section 8.2 as sample drafting language, not a verbatim-language mandate.
process.quote: Violations must be reported to FEMA and the Regional Office of the Environmental Protection Agency.

requirements.statement: This edition (Version 2, effective October 1, 2024) applies only to FEMA awards made or disasters declared on or after October 1, 2024.
requirements.quote: This document applies to all FEMA awards made or disasters declared on or after October 1, 2024

requirements.statement: The federal award date or the disaster declaration date determines which federal procurement standards and required contract provisions apply.
requirements.quote: this date determines the applicable federal procurement standards including the required contract provisions in 2 C.F.R. Part 200

requirements.statement: For awards made or disasters declared between November 12, 2020 and September 30, 2024, the June 2021 Guide applies instead of this edition.
requirements.quote: For FEMA awards made or disasters declared between November 12, 2020, through September 30, 2024, please refer to the Contract Provisions Guide dated June 2021

requirements.statement: Applicability of the provisions depends on circumstances such as the type of work being procured, the dollar amount, and the procurement date.
requirements.quote: Many of the provisions described in this document only apply when certain circumstances are present, such as the type of work being procured, the dollar amount, or the date when it is procured.

requirements.statement: The Guide does not provide contract provisions required by state, tribal, or local law. Outputs therefore express no opinion on non-federal duties.
requirements.quote: Contract provisions required by applicable state, tribal, or local laws or rules separate from the federal procurement standards.

requirements.statement: The recipient or subrecipient is solely responsible for ensuring that its contract language meets 2 C.F.R. Part 200 requirements.
requirements.quote: The recipient or subrecipient is solely responsible for ensuring that all language included in its contracts meets the requirements of 2 C.F.R. Part 200

requirements.statement: A contract is a legal instrument by which a FEMA award recipient or subrecipient purchases property or services needed to carry out the project or program under a federal award.
requirements.quote: A legal instrument by which a FEMA award recipient or subrecipient purchases property or services needed to carry out the project or program under a federal award

requirements.statement: Construction work is defined by reference to 41 C.F.R. § 60-1.3. It includes construction, rehabilitation, alteration, conversion, extension, demolition, or repair of buildings, highways, or other improvements to real property.
requirements.quote: The regulation at 41 C.F.R. § 60-1.3 defines construction work as

requirements.statement: Contracts must address termination for cause and for convenience by the recipient or subrecipient, including how termination will be carried out and the basis for settlement.
requirements.quote: Contracts must address termination for cause and for convenience by the recipient or subrecipient, including the manner by which it will be carried out and the basis for settlement

requirements.statement: The termination provision is required for contracts and purchase orders that exceed $10,000.
requirements.quote: This contract provision is required for contracts and purchase orders exceeding $10,000.

requirements.statement: For contracts at or below $10,000, FEMA suggests a termination for cause provision, but it is not required.
requirements.quote: For contracts at or below $10,000, FEMA suggests including a termination for cause provision, but this is not required.

requirements.statement: FEMA recommends that termination clauses be actionable and specific. This is a recommendation, not an applicability condition.
requirements.quote: FEMA recommends that termination clauses be actionable and specific.

requirements.statement: When the federal program legislation requires it, every prime construction contract over $2,000 must include a Davis-Bacon Act compliance provision.
requirements.quote: When required by the federal program legislation, all prime construction contracts over $2,000 awarded by recipients or subrecipients must include a provision for compliance with the Davis-Bacon Act

requirements.statement: The Davis-Bacon Act does not apply to all FEMA financial assistance programs.
requirements.quote: The Davis-Bacon Act does not apply to all FEMA financial assistance programs.

requirements.statement: To determine whether the Davis-Bacon provision is required for a procurement, recipients should consult the NOFO or other program guidance, or contact the FEMA grant representative.
requirements.quote: Recipients and subrecipients should refer to applicable NOFO or other program guidance or contact their applicable FEMA grant representative to determine if this provision is required for the procurement.

requirements.statement: Exception: the Davis-Bacon clause is not federally required for procurements under FEMA Public Assistance (PA) or Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) programs. This exception takes precedence over the general rule.
requirements.quote: However, the Davis-Bacon Act clause is not federally required for procurements under FEMA’s Public Assistance (PA) or Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) Programs.

requirements.statement: If Davis-Bacon applies, contracts or subcontracts must be awarded on the condition that the prevailing wage determination is accepted.
requirements.quote: Contracts or subcontracts must be awarded on the condition that the prevailing wage determination is accepted.

requirements.statement: If Davis-Bacon applies, the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) must be included in full in all applicable contracts.
requirements.quote: the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) in full into all applicable contracts

requirements.statement: Contracts subject to the Davis-Bacon Act must also include a Copeland Anti-Kickback Act compliance provision.
requirements.quote: Contracts subject to the Davis-Bacon Act, must also include a provision for compliance with the Copeland

requirements.statement: Each contractor must base wages for every mechanic and laborer on a standard 40-hour work week.
requirements.quote: Under 40 U.S.C. § 3702, each contractor must base wages for every mechanic and laborer on a standard 40-hour work week.

requirements.statement: The work-hours and safety provision applies to procurements over $100,000 that involve the employment of mechanics or laborers and construction work.
requirements.quote: This required contract provision applies to all procurements over $100,000 that involve the employment of mechanics, laborers, and construction work

requirements.statement: Exception: the requirements do not apply to purchases of supplies, materials, or articles ordinarily available on the open market, or to contracts for transportation or transmission of intelligence.
requirements.quote: These requirements do not apply to the purchase of supplies, materials, or articles ordinarily available on the open market, contracts for transportation or transmission of intelligence

requirements.statement: If applicable, the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5) must be included verbatim in all applicable contracts.
requirements.quote: If applicable per the standard described above, the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5), verbatim, into all applicable contracts

requirements.statement: For contracts subject only to the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act, a clause meeting 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(c) must also be inserted. Specific language is not required.
requirements.quote: the recipient or subrecipient must also insert a clause meeting the requirements of 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(c)

requirements.statement: Contracts must contain a provision requiring contractors to comply with the Clean Air Act and the Federal Water Pollution Control Act.
requirements.quote: Contracts must contain a provision requiring contractors to comply with the Clean Air Act

requirements.statement: Violations must be reported to FEMA and to the Regional Office of the EPA.
requirements.quote: Violations must be reported to FEMA and the Regional Office of the Environmental Protection Agency

requirements.statement: The Clean Air/Water provision is required for all procurements over $150,000.
requirements.quote: This contract provision is required for all procurements over $150,000.

requirements.statement: The sample (suggested, not mandated) language flows the requirements down to each subcontract exceeding $150,000.
requirements.quote: The contractor agrees to include these requirements in each subcontract exceeding $150,000 financed in whole or in part with federal assistance provided by FEMA.

process.action: Confirm the award or declaration date falls on or after 2024-10-01 so that this edition governs. Otherwise, stop and use the earlier edition.
process.quote: This document applies to all FEMA awards made or disasters declared on or after October 1, 2024

process.action: Gather the case facts: contract amount, type of work and category, FEMA program, program-legislation Davis-Bacon applicability, and employment of mechanics or laborers.
process.quote: Many of the provisions described in this document only apply when certain circumstances are present, such as the type of work being procured, the dollar amount, or the date when it is procured.

process.action: Termination (section 2.1): if the amount exceeds $10,000, the provision is required. If the amount is at or below $10,000, it is suggested but not required.
process.quote: This contract provision is required for contracts and purchase orders exceeding $10,000.

process.action: Davis-Bacon (section 4.1): first apply the exception. If the program is PA or HMA, the clause is not federally required.
process.quote: However, the Davis-Bacon Act clause is not federally required for procurements under FEMA’s Public Assistance (PA) or Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) Programs.

process.quote: When required by the federal program legislation, all prime construction contracts over $2,000 awarded by recipients or subrecipients must include a provision for compliance with the Davis-Bacon Act

process.action: Davis-Bacon: if program-legislation applicability is unknown, or the contract's construction status is uncharacterised, keep the result unknown. Consult the NOFO, program guidance, or the FEMA grant representative.
process.quote: Recipients and subrecipients should refer to applicable NOFO or other program guidance or contact their applicable FEMA grant representative to determine if this provision is required for the procurement.

process.action: Work hours (section 6.1): first apply the exclusions for open-market supplies, transportation, and transmission of intelligence.
process.quote: These requirements do not apply to the purchase of supplies, materials, or articles ordinarily available on the open market, contracts for transportation or transmission of intelligence

process.action: Work hours: for non-excluded procurements, the provision is required when the amount is over $100,000 and the procurement involves mechanics or laborers and construction work. Uncharacterised other work stays unknown.
process.quote: This required contract provision applies to all procurements over $100,000 that involve the employment of mechanics, laborers, and construction work

process.action: Clean Air/Water (section 8.1): the provision is required if the amount is over $150,000.
process.quote: This contract provision is required for all procurements over $150,000.

process.action: For each provision found required, the recipient or subrecipient ensures the contract language meets 2 C.F.R. Part 200. This draft remains unapproved pending that review.

requirements.statement: Offerors are responsible for submitting proposals, revisions and modifications so that they reach the Government office designated in the solicitation by the time the solicitation specifies.
requirements.quote: Offerors are responsible for submitting proposals, and any revisions, and modifications, so as to reach the Government office designated in the solicitation by the time specified in the solicitation.

requirements.statement: Offerors may use any transmission method that the solicitation authorizes, such as regular mail, electronic commerce or facsimile.
requirements.quote: Offerors may use any transmission method authorized by the solicitation (i.e., regular mail, electronic commerce, or facsimile).

requirements.statement: If the solicitation specifies no time, the receipt time is 4:30 p.m. local time for the designated Government office on the due date.
requirements.quote: If no time is specified in the solicitation, the time for receipt is 4:30 p.m., local time, for the designated Government office on the date that proposals are due.

requirements.statement: When electronic commerce is used to receive proposals, modifications and revisions, the RFP must specify which electronic commerce methods offerors may use. This defines what counts as an authorized electronic method under 15.208(b)(1)(i).
requirements.quote: In this case, the RFP shall specify the electronic commerce method(s) that offerors may use

requirements.statement: A proposal, modification or revision is late if the designated Government office receives it after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals.
requirements.quote: Any proposal, modification, or revision, that is received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is

requirements.statement: A late item will not be considered unless all of the following hold: it is received before award, the contracting officer determines that accepting it would not unduly delay the acquisition, and one of the exceptions in (b)(1)(i) to (iii) applies.
requirements.quote: will not be considered unless it is received before award is made, the contracting officer determines that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition

requirements.statement: Exception (b)(1)(i): the item was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the solicitation, and it reached the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure no later than 5:00 p.m. one working day before the date specified for receipt of proposals. Implementation choice, not source text: 5:00 p.m. is treated as inclusive (minute 1020). Gateway receipt two or more working days before the due date also satisfies 'not later than'.
requirements.quote: If it was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the solicitation, it was received at the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure not later than 5:00 p.m. one working day prior to the date specified for receipt of proposals

requirements.statement: Exception (b)(1)(ii): acceptable evidence establishes that the Government installation designated for receipt received the item and that the item was under Government control before the time set for receipt.
requirements.quote: There is acceptable evidence to establish that it was received at the Government installation designated for receipt of proposals and was under the Government

requirements.statement: Exception (b)(1)(iii): the late item was the only proposal received.
requirements.quote: It was the only proposal received.

requirements.statement: A late modification of an otherwise successful proposal that makes its terms more favorable to the Government will be considered whenever it is received. This rule is introduced by 'However' and overrides the (b)(1) limits on award timing, undue delay and the listed exceptions.
requirements.quote: However, a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted.

requirements.statement: Such a favorable late modification of an otherwise successful proposal may be accepted. Acceptance is permitted, not required.
requirements.quote: will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted

requirements.statement: Acceptable evidence of the time of receipt at the Government installation includes any of the following: the installation's time/date stamp on the proposal wrapper, other documentary evidence of receipt kept by the installation, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.
requirements.quote: Acceptable evidence to establish the time of receipt at the Government installation includes the time/date stamp of that installation on the proposal wrapper, other documentary evidence of receipt maintained by the installation, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.

requirements.statement: The emergency extension is triggered only when all three conditions hold: an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes; as a result, proposals cannot be received at the designated office by the exact specified time; and urgent Government requirements preclude amending the closing date.
requirements.quote: If an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes so that proposals cannot be received at the Government office designated for receipt of proposals by the exact time specified in the solicitation, and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the solicitation closing date

requirements.statement: When triggered, the receipt time is deemed extended to the same time of day specified in the solicitation, on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume. No specific date is fixed by the source.
requirements.quote: the time specified for receipt of proposals will be deemed to be extended to the same time of day specified in the solicitation on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume.

requirements.statement: Proposals may be withdrawn by written notice at any time before award.
requirements.quote: Proposals may be withdrawn by written notice at any time before award.

requirements.statement: Oral proposals made in response to oral solicitations may be withdrawn orally.
requirements.quote: Oral proposals in response to oral solicitations may be withdrawn orally.

requirements.statement: The contracting officer must document the contract file when oral withdrawals are made.
requirements.quote: The contracting officer must document the contract file when oral withdrawals are made.

requirements.statement: One copy of a withdrawn proposal should be retained in the contract file. This is hortatory ('should') rather than a mandatory duty.
requirements.quote: One copy of withdrawn proposals should be retained in the contract file

requirements.statement: Extra copies of withdrawn proposals may be destroyed or returned to the offeror at the offeror's request.
requirements.quote: Extra copies of the withdrawn proposals may be destroyed or returned to the offeror at the offeror

requirements.statement: Where practicable, withdrawn electronically transmitted proposals must be purged from primary and backup data storage after a copy is made for the file.
requirements.quote: Where practicable, electronically transmitted proposals that are withdrawn must be purged from primary and backup data storage systems after a copy is made for the file.

requirements.statement: Extremely bulky proposals must be returned only at the offeror's request and expense.
requirements.quote: Extremely bulky proposals must only be returned at the offeror

requirements.statement: The contracting officer must promptly notify an offeror whose proposal, modification or revision was received late, and must tell the offeror whether its proposal will be considered.
requirements.quote: The contracting officer must promptly notify any offeror if its proposal, modification, or revision was received late, and must inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered

requirements.statement: Exception to the late-receipt notice duty: no notice is required when contract award is imminent and the 15.503(b) notice would suffice. Both conditions must hold.
requirements.quote: unless contract award is imminent and the notice prescribed in 15.503(b) would suffice.

requirements.statement: The 15.503(b) postaward notice referenced by the late-notice exception: within 3 days after award, the contracting officer gives written notice to each offeror whose proposal was in the competitive range but not selected, or who had not been notified earlier under 15.503(a). This is cited only as the notice referenced in 15.208(f).
requirements.quote: Within 3 days after the date of contract award, the contracting officer shall provide written notification to each offeror whose proposal was in the competitive range but was not selected for award

requirements.statement: Late proposals and modifications that are not considered must be held unopened until after award, unless opened for identification, and then retained with other unsuccessful proposals.
requirements.quote: Late proposals and modifications that are not considered must be held unopened, unless opened for identification, until after award and then retained with other unsuccessful proposals.

requirements.statement: If available, specified records must be placed in the contracting office files for each late proposal, modification or revision, and for each withdrawal.
requirements.quote: If available, the following must be included in the contracting office files for each late proposal, modification, revision, or withdrawal:

requirements.statement: The file must include the date and hour of receipt, if available.
requirements.quote: The date and hour of receipt.

requirements.statement: The file must include a statement, with supporting rationale, on whether the item was considered for award, if available.
requirements.quote: A statement regarding whether the proposal was considered for award, with supporting rationale.

requirements.statement: The file must include the envelope, wrapper or other evidence of date of receipt, if available.
requirements.quote: The envelope, wrapper, or other evidence of date of receipt.

requirements.statement: On receipt at the location specified in the solicitation, proposals must be marked with the date and time of receipt and sent to the designated officials.
requirements.quote: Upon receipt at the location specified in the solicitation, proposals and information received in response to a request for information (RFI) shall be marked with the date and time of receipt and shall be transmitted to the designated officials.

requirements.statement: If any portion of a proposal received electronically or by facsimile is unreadable, the contracting officer must immediately notify the offeror and allow it to resubmit that portion.
requirements.quote: If any portion of a proposal received by the contracting officer electronically or by facsimile is unreadable, the contracting officer immediately shall notify the offeror and permit the offeror to resubmit the unreadable portion of the proposal.

requirements.statement: The contracting officer prescribes the method and time for resubmission after consulting the offeror, and documents them in the file.
requirements.quote: The method and time for resubmission shall be prescribed by the contracting officer after consultation with the offeror, and documented in the file.

requirements.statement: A resubmission is treated as received at the date and time of the original unreadable submission for 15.208(a) timeliness. This applies only if the offeror meets the prescribed resubmission time and format requirements.
requirements.quote: The resubmission shall be considered as if it were received at the date and time of the original unreadable submission for the purpose of determining timeliness under 15.208(a), provided the offeror complies with the time and format requirements for resubmission prescribed by the contracting officer.

requirements.quote: Proposal modification is a change made to a proposal before the solicitation closing date and time, or made in response to an amendment, or made to correct a mistake at any time before award.

requirements.quote: Proposal revision is a change to a proposal made after the solicitation closing date, at the request of or as allowed by a contracting officer, as the result of negotiations.

requirements.statement: Oral presentations are subject to the same timing restrictions (15.208) as written information.
requirements.quote: are subject to the same restrictions as written information, regarding timing (see 15.208)

requirements.quote: The contracting officer is required to establish a common cut-off date only for receipt of final proposal revisions.
