requirements.statement: For the ordinary late-item exception, the contracting officer must determine that accepting the late item would not unduly delay the acquisition.
requirements.quote: the contracting officer determines that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition

requirements.statement: The electronic alternative requires a solicitation-authorized electronic commerce method and receipt at the initial Government infrastructure entry point no later than 5:00 p.m. one working day before the proposal due date. Earlier working days also satisfy that cutoff.
requirements.quote: If it was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the solicitation, it was received at the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure not later than 5:00 p.m. one working day prior to the date specified for receipt of proposals

requirements.statement: The Government-installation alternative requires acceptable evidence establishing both receipt at the installation designated for proposals and Government control before the receipt deadline.
requirements.quote: There is acceptable evidence to establish that it was received at the Government installation designated for receipt of proposals and was under the Government’s control prior to the time set for receipt of proposals

requirements.statement: Acceptable installation-receipt evidence includes the installation's time/date stamp on the proposal wrapper, other installation-maintained documentary receipt evidence, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel. The listed forms are inclusive, not an exclusive list.
requirements.quote: Acceptable evidence to establish the time of receipt at the Government installation includes the time/date stamp of that installation on the proposal wrapper, other documentary evidence of receipt maintained by the installation, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.

requirements.statement: Being the only proposal received is an alternative under the ordinary late-item exception; receipt before award and the no-undue-delay determination still apply.
requirements.quote: It was the only proposal received.

requirements.statement: Consider a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal that makes its terms more favorable to the Government at any time it is received. This special rule is not subject to the ordinary preaward, no-undue-delay, gateway, installation-control, or only-proposal conditions.
requirements.quote: However, a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted.

requirements.statement: A late modification satisfying 15.208(b)(2) may be accepted. The required consideration output does not decide acceptance or award.
requirements.quote: will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted.

requirements.statement: The deemed emergency extension triggers when an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes, that interruption prevents timely receipt at the designated Government office, and urgent Government requirements preclude amending the closing date.
requirements.quote: If an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes so that proposals cannot be received at the Government office designated for receipt of proposals by the exact time specified in the solicitation, and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the solicitation closing date

requirements.statement: When 15.208(d) triggers, the extended deadline is the same specified time of day on the first workday on which normal Government processes resume. No particular calendar date is established by the supplied inputs.
requirements.quote: the time specified for receipt of proposals will be deemed to be extended to the same time of day specified in the solicitation on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume.

requirements.statement: Promptly notify an offeror when its proposal, modification, or revision was received late, unless both elements of the 15.208(f) notice exception apply. This duty does not depend on whether the item can be considered.
requirements.quote: The contracting officer must promptly notify any offeror if its proposal, modification, or revision was received late, and must inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered, unless contract award is imminent and the notice prescribed in 15.503(b) would suffice.

requirements.statement: When the prompt late-receipt notice is required, inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered.
requirements.quote: must inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered, unless contract award is imminent and the notice prescribed in 15.503(b) would suffice.

requirements.statement: The 15.208(f) prompt-notice exception requires both imminent contract award and sufficiency of the notice prescribed in 15.503(b). Sufficiency is an externally supplied procedural fact, not inferred from imminence.
requirements.quote: unless contract award is imminent and the notice prescribed in 15.503(b) would suffice.

requirements.statement: Hold late proposals and modifications that are not considered unopened until after award, subject to opening for identification. This paragraph expressly names proposals and modifications, not revisions.
requirements.quote: Late proposals and modifications that are not considered must be held unopened, unless opened for identification, until after award

requirements.statement: After award, retain unconsidered late proposals and modifications with other unsuccessful proposals.
requirements.quote: and then retained with other unsuccessful proposals.

requirements.statement: For each late proposal, modification, or revision in the interface scope, include its receipt date and hour in the contracting office files if available.
requirements.quote: If available, the following must be included in the contracting office files for each late proposal, modification, revision, or withdrawal: (1) The date and hour of receipt.

requirements.statement: For each late proposal, modification, or revision in scope, include a statement of whether the proposal was considered for award and the supporting rationale, if available. Eligibility for consideration is not itself a finding that actual consideration for award occurred.
requirements.quote: (2) A statement regarding whether the proposal was considered for award, with supporting rationale.

requirements.statement: For each late proposal, modification, or revision in scope, include the envelope, wrapper, or other evidence of receipt date in the contracting office files if available.
requirements.quote: (3) The envelope, wrapper, or other evidence of date of receipt.

process.action: Implementation context, not an additional FAR obligation: treat this blueprint as an unapproved model draft for the supplied FAR Part 15 edition, FAC 2026-01, effective 2026-03-13. Limit the three outputs to 15.208(b), (f), and (d), respectively, with related receipt-evidence, custody, and file procedures. Use the supplied typed case facts without inventing additional inputs. Rule ordering and unknown defaults are implementation choices; substantive conditions and exceptions come from the cited source.
process.quote: 15.208 Submission, modification, revision, and withdrawal of proposals.

process.action: Assess the emergency extension independently of whether this item is late: require process_interrupted, interruption_prevents_timely_receipt, and urgent_needs_preclude_amendment all to be true. If triggered, preserve the extended deadline as the same specified time of day on the first workday normal Government processes resume. Do not invent a resumption date or require an actual solicitation amendment for this deemed extension.
process.quote: If an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes so that proposals cannot be received at the Government office designated for receipt of proposals by the exact time specified in the solicitation, and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the solicitation closing date, the time specified for receipt of proposals will be deemed to be extended to the same time of day specified in the solicitation on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume.

process.action: Use received_late as the supplied determination of receipt after the effective deadline; it already incorporates any applicable emergency extension. Do not recompute or reverse that fact from P02. For an on-time item, return unknown for late_submission_considerable because the output addresses only late-item exceptions.
process.quote: Any proposal, modification, or revision, that is received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is "late"

process.action: For a late item, first test the special modification rule: item_kind must be modification, otherwise_successful_proposal must be true, and modified_terms_more_favourable must be true. If satisfied, the item must be considered at any receipt time. Give this rule precedence over all ordinary exception gates. Keep permission to accept distinct from the consideration result.
process.quote: However, a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted.

process.action: If the late item does not satisfy P04, require receipt before award and a contracting officer determination that acceptance would not unduly delay the acquisition. Failure of either condition defeats the ordinary exception, without overriding P04.
process.quote: will not be considered unless it is received before award is made, the contracting officer determines that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition

process.action: Where installation receipt is relied on, use acceptable_receipt_evidence as the supplied acceptability fact and check both designated_installation_received_before_deadline and government_control_before_deadline. Source-recognized evidence includes installation stamps, other installation-maintained documentary evidence, and Government personnel testimony or statements; do not impose a documentary-only restriction.
process.quote: Acceptable evidence to establish the time of receipt at the Government installation includes the time/date stamp of that installation on the proposal wrapper, other documentary evidence of receipt maintained by the installation, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.

process.action: For an item passing the ordinary gates, require at least one alternative: authorized electronic transmission received before the preceding-working-day cutoff; acceptable evidence of designated-installation receipt and Government control before the deadline; or only_proposal_received. Implement the electronic cutoff as gateway_workdays_before_due_date greater than 1, or equal to 1 with gateway_minute_of_day at most 1020. Do not impose the electronic method requirement on the other alternatives or require multiple alternatives simultaneously. If no alternative applies, the late item is not considerable under the scoped exceptions.
process.quote: (i) If it was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the solicitation, it was received at the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure not later than 5:00 p.m. one working day prior to the date specified for receipt of proposals; or (ii) There is acceptable evidence to establish that it was received at the Government installation designated for receipt of proposals and was under the Government’s control prior to the time set for receipt of proposals; or (iii) It was the only proposal received.

process.action: Determine the prompt late-receipt notice duty independently of consideration eligibility. No duty under this paragraph is triggered for an on-time item. For a late proposal, modification, or revision, promptly notify the offeror and state whether the proposal will be considered, unless contract_award_imminent and award_notice_would_suffice are both true. Use the supplied sufficiency fact without importing additional notice tests or deciding duties under other sections.
process.quote: The contracting officer must promptly notify any offeror if its proposal, modification, or revision was received late, and must inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered, unless contract award is imminent and the notice prescribed in 15.503(b) would suffice.

process.action: For a late proposal or modification that is not considered, hold it unopened until after award unless opening is necessary for identification, then retain it with other unsuccessful proposals. Do not automatically extend paragraph (g)'s expressly named item categories to revisions.
process.quote: Late proposals and modifications that are not considered must be held unopened, unless opened for identification, until after award and then retained with other unsuccessful proposals.

process.action: For each late proposal, modification, or revision in scope, include available receipt date and hour, the actual consideration-for-award statement and supporting rationale, and the envelope, wrapper, or other receipt-date evidence in the contracting office files. Preserve the if-available qualification. Record the applicable exception or failed ordinary conditions as appropriate, without equating eligibility for consideration with acceptance or award.
process.quote: If available, the following must be included in the contracting office files for each late proposal, modification, revision, or withdrawal: (1) The date and hour of receipt. (2) A statement regarding whether the proposal was considered for award, with supporting rationale. (3) The envelope, wrapper, or other evidence of date of receipt.

requirements.statement: The circular applies to any recipient procurement that uses FTA financial assistance, unless FTA specifies otherwise in writing.
requirements.quote: This guidance, unless otherwise specified by FTA in writing, applies whenever a recipient uses FTA financial assistance for its procurement activities.

requirements.statement: Precedence: where the circular is inconsistent with changes in a statute or regulation, the statute or regulation supersedes the circular. The circular is applicable as of January 17, 2025.
requirements.quote: In cases where this circular is inconsistent with changes in any statute or regulation, the statute or regulation will supersede this circular. This circular is applicable as of January 17, 2025.

requirements.statement: The date of an award, or of an amendment adding funds, may determine which regulatory requirements apply. This is why effective thresholds are supplied as case inputs.
requirements.quote: The date of an award or amendment adding funds may determine the application of the specific regulatory requirements.

requirements.statement: Interpretive rule: mandatory terms (must/shall) describe binding requirements. Permissive terms (may/should) are non-binding guidance that permits discretion.
requirements.quote: should be interpreted only as non-binding guidance, recommendations, or best practices, and permit discretion.

requirements.statement: 2 CFR Part 200 incorporates the FAR simplified acquisition threshold and micro-purchase threshold, which may be updated at 48 CFR Part 2. The blueprint does not hardcode these values. Effective thresholds are supplied inputs.
requirements.quote: The Uniform Administrative Requirements (2 CFR Part 200) also incorporate the simplified acquisition threshold and micro-purchase threshold established in the FAR. This threshold may be updated at 48 CFR Part 2.

requirements.statement: The source states a simplified acquisition threshold value as of a specific date. This is a dated reference only and is not used as a hardcoded rule constant.
requirements.quote: Contracts for more than the simplified acquisition threshold ($250,000, as of October 1, 2024)

requirements.statement: The recipient shall conduct all procurement transactions under an FTA award in a manner that provides full and open competition.
requirements.quote: The recipient shall conduct all procurement transactions under an FTA award in a manner that provides full and open competition.

requirements.statement: The recipient must use competitive procedures appropriate for the acquisition. Those procedures must comply with State and local law and with Federal requirements.
requirements.quote: The recipient must use competitive procedures appropriate for the acquisition undertaken. The procedures used must comply with State and local law as well as with Federal requirements.

requirements.statement: The recipient may acquire property and services without competitive quotations only if all of the following are met: (a) State and local law permit it; (b) the value is at or below the current micro-purchase threshold; (c) the recipient considers the price reasonable based on research, experience, purchase history, or other information; and (d) the recipient maintains documents supporting that conclusion.
requirements.quote: If permitted by State and local law, the recipient may acquire property and services valued at or below the current micro-purchase threshold without obtaining competitive quotations if the recipient considers the price reasonable based on research, experience, purchase history, or other information, and maintains documents to support its conclusion.

requirements.statement: The Federal micro-purchase threshold is established in 2 CFR 200.1 and 48 CFR 2.101. The recipient may set for itself a lower or higher micro-purchase threshold.
requirements.quote: The Federal micro-purchase threshold is established in 2 CFR 200.1; 48 CFR 2.101. The recipient may set for itself a lower or higher micro-purchase threshold.

requirements.statement: The recipient may self-certify a micro-purchase threshold up to $50,000.
requirements.quote: Pursuant to 2 CFR 200.320(a)(1), the recipient may self-certify a micro-purchase threshold up to $50,000.

requirements.statement: The recipient must act on an annual basis and must maintain documentation available to FTA and auditors under 2 CFR 200.334. The source sentence omits the annual action's verb. Treating it as annual self-certification is an interpretation, not a stated fact.
requirements.quote: The recipient must on an annual basis and must maintain documentation to be made available to FTA and auditors in accordance with 2 CFR 200.334.

requirements.statement: The self-certification must include a justification and a clear identification of the threshold. It must also include supporting documentation of at least one of: (a) low-risk auditee qualification under 2 CFR 200.520 for the most recent audit; (b) an annual internal institutional risk assessment; or (c) for public institutions, consistency of a higher threshold with State law.
requirements.quote: The self-certification must include a justification, clear identification of the threshold, and supporting documentation of any of the following: a qualification as a low-risk auditee, in accordance with the criteria in 2 CFR 200.520 for the most recent audit; an annual internal institutional risk assessment to identify, mitigate, and manage financial risks; or, for public institutions, a higher threshold is consistent with State law.

requirements.actor: Recipient; cognizant agency for indirect costs
requirements.statement: A micro-purchase threshold higher than $50,000 must be approved by the recipient's cognizant agency for indirect costs. Thresholds of $50,000 or below fall within the self-certification permission instead.
requirements.quote: A micro-purchase threshold higher than $50,000 must be approved by the recipient’s cognizant agency for indirect costs.

requirements.statement: To the extent practicable, the recipient should distribute micro-purchases equitably among qualified suppliers. This is non-binding guidance.
requirements.quote: to the extent practicable, the recipient should distribute micro-purchases equitably among qualified suppliers.

requirements.statement: The recipient may not divide or reduce the size of its procurement merely to come within the micro-purchase limit.
requirements.quote: The recipient may not divide or reduce the size of its procurement merely to come within the micro-purchase limit.

requirements.statement: For a micro-purchase, the recipient must maintain documents supporting its consideration that the price is reasonable.
requirements.quote: The recipient must maintain documents to support its consideration that the micro-purchase price is reasonable based on research, experience, purchase history, or other information, as required under 2 CFR 200.320(a)(1)(ii).

requirements.statement: Exception for micro-purchases: the recipient need not justify the procurement method, contract type, or contractor selection or rejection. This takes precedence over the general procurement-history record requirement in R19.
requirements.quote: The recipient need not justify the procurement method used, selection of contract type, or reasons for contractor selection or rejection.

requirements.statement: General rule: recipients must document the rationale for the procurement method used for each contract. Micro-purchases are relieved of this justification under R18.
requirements.quote: Recipients must document the rationale for the procurement method used for each contract.

requirements.statement: Simplified acquisition procedures are authorized when the aggregate dollar amount is higher than the micro-purchase threshold and does not exceed the simplified acquisition threshold.
requirements.quote: 2 CFR 200.320(a)(2) authorizes simplified acquisition procedures when the aggregate dollar amount of the procurement transaction is higher than the micro-purchase threshold but does not exceed the simplified acquisition threshold as defined in 2 CFR 200.1; 48 CFR 2.101.

requirements.statement: The recipient may set a lower threshold for simplified acquisition procedures.
requirements.quote: The recipient may set a lower threshold for simplified acquisition procedures.

requirements.statement: The recipient may not set a simplified acquisition threshold higher than the Federal threshold.
requirements.quote: 2 CFR 200.320 does not permit a recipient to set a simplified acquisition threshold higher than the Federal threshold.

requirements.statement: When using simplified acquisition procedures, the recipient must obtain price or rate quotations from an adequate number of qualified sources. The recipient may use judgment on what number is adequate.
requirements.quote: The recipient must obtain price or rate quotations from an adequate number of qualified sources. The recipient may exercise judgment in determining what number is adequate.

requirements.statement: The recipient may not divide or reduce the size of its procurement to avoid the additional procurement requirements applicable to larger acquisitions.
requirements.quote: The recipient may not divide or reduce the size of its procurement to avoid the additional procurement requirements applicable to larger acquisitions.

requirements.statement: For simplified acquisitions, the recipient must maintain records supporting: (a) the decision to use the procedure; (b) the contract type; (c) the sources solicited; and (d) the reasons for contractor selection or rejection.
requirements.quote: The recipient must maintain records to support its decision to use the simplified acquisition procedure, the selection of contract type, the sources solicited, and the reasons for contractor selection or rejection.

requirements.statement: Under the exceptions to full and open competition, micro-purchase procedures that do not require competition may be used when the aggregate amount does not exceed the micro-purchase threshold.
requirements.quote: When the aggregate amount of the procurement transaction does not exceed the micro-purchase threshold

requirements.statement: A recipient must not divide a known requirement into smaller purchases for the purpose of avoiding competition requirements.
requirements.quote: A recipient must not divide a known requirement into smaller purchases for the purpose of avoiding competition requirements.

requirements.statement: The recipient should consider consolidating or breaking out a procurement for economy. Breaking out procurements may be legitimate, for example to increase DBE and small-business participation. Splitting is therefore not prohibited in itself; only the stated anti-avoidance purpose is prohibited.
requirements.quote: The recipient should consider whether to consolidate or break out the procurement to obtain a more economical purchase.

requirements.statement: Legitimate break-outs are recognized as able to provide opportunities for DBEs and other small firms.
requirements.quote: In other circumstances, breaking out procurements may provide greater opportunities for Disadvantaged Business Enterprises (DBEs)

requirements.statement: Guidance: a recipient should not split a large procurement merely to use the informal methods available below the simplified acquisition or micro-purchase thresholds.
requirements.quote: However, a recipient should not split a large procurement merely to take advantage of the informal procurement methods available for procurements below the simplified acquisition threshold or micro-purchase threshold.

requirements.statement: A cost or price analysis is required for every procurement action above the simplified acquisition threshold, including contract modifications and option exercises.
requirements.quote: 2 CFR 200.324 requires the recipient to perform a cost analysis or price analysis in connection with every procurement action, including contract modifications and options exercises, in excess of the simplified acquisition threshold.

requirements.statement: Reverse auctions may be used only for procurements at or below the simplified acquisition threshold.
requirements.quote: Recipients may use reverse auctions only for procurements at or below the simplified acquisition threshold.

requirements.statement: Documentation should be commensurate with the procurement. For example, a receipt may suffice for a small credit card purchase.
requirements.quote: For example, a receipt or bill accompanying a $100 credit card purchase might contain all the required information to support that procurement.

requirements.statement: If Federal requirements conflict with State or local requirements, the recipient should promptly notify the FTA regional office in writing.
requirements.quote: If Federal requirements conflict with State or local requirements, the recipient should promptly provide written notification to the FTA regional office responsible for administering its award.

requirements.statement: A State or Indian Tribe must use the same procurement policies and procedures it uses for acquisitions not financed with Federal assistance.
requirements.quote: a State or Indian Tribe must use the same procurement policies and procedures that it uses for acquisitions not financed with Federal assistance.

requirements.statement: Recipients are required to self-certify annually that their procurement systems comply with Federal regulations.
requirements.quote: Recipients are required to annually self-certify that their procurement systems are in compliance with Federal regulations

process.action: If the recipient proposes its own micro-purchase threshold: a threshold up to $50,000 may be self-certified with a justification, threshold identification and supporting documentation; a threshold above $50,000 requires cognizant-agency approval.

process.action: Determine the aggregate amount of the procurement transaction. Check whether any division or reduction was made merely to come within the micro-purchase limit or to avoid larger-acquisition requirements.

process.action: For micro-purchases: maintain price-reasonableness documentation, and distribute purchases equitably among qualified suppliers where practicable. Method, contract-type and selection justifications are not required.
process.quote: The recipient need not justify the procurement method used, selection of contract type, or reasons for contractor selection or rejection.

requirements.statement: The interpretive baseline is the supplied January 17, 2025 edition of Circular 4220.1G, applicable as of that date. This blueprint does not substitute subsequent law or another edition.
requirements.quote: This circular is applicable as of January 17, 2025.

requirements.statement: The circular is guidance rather than Federal law or regulation. Its mandatory terms describe binding requirements; its permissive terms describe non-binding guidance, recommendations, or best practices.
requirements.quote: This circular will use the terms “must” or “shall” or similarly mandatory terms when describing a requirement that is binding by law or by operation of a financial assistance agreement with FTA. Permissive terms like “may” or “should” should be interpreted only as non-binding guidance, recommendations, or best practices, and permit discretion.

requirements.statement: Where the circular conflicts with changes in a statute or regulation, the statute or regulation supersedes the circular. No external change is inferred in this fixed-edition blueprint.
requirements.quote: In cases where this circular is inconsistent with changes in any statute or regulation, the statute or regulation will supersede this circular.

requirements.statement: Use procurement procedures appropriate to the acquisition that comply with State and local law and Federal requirements.
requirements.quote: The recipient must use competitive procedures appropriate for the acquisition undertaken. The procedures used must comply with State and local law as well as with Federal requirements.

requirements.statement: The VI.3.a(1) micro-purchase route requires State and local law to permit its use.
requirements.quote: If permitted by State and local law, the recipient may acquire property and services

requirements.statement: The micro-purchase amount condition includes equality: the transaction must be at or below the applicable effective micro-purchase threshold.
requirements.quote: property and services valued at or below the current micro-purchase threshold

requirements.statement: Under VI.3.a(1), a recipient may purchase without competitive quotations when State and local law permit, the amount is at or below its applicable micro-purchase threshold, the recipient considers the price reasonable on an allowed basis, and supporting documents are maintained. This permission does not override the prohibited-division provisions.
requirements.quote: If permitted by State and local law, the recipient may acquire property and services valued at or below the current micro-purchase threshold without obtaining competitive quotations if the recipient considers the price reasonable based on research, experience, purchase history, or other information, and maintains documents to support its conclusion.

requirements.statement: Maintain documents supporting the conclusion that a micro-purchase price is reasonable based on research, experience, purchase history, or other information.
requirements.quote: The recipient must maintain documents to support its consideration that the micro-purchase price is reasonable based on research, experience, purchase history, or other information, as required under 2 CFR 200.320(a)(1)(ii).

requirements.statement: A recipient may establish a lower or higher micro-purchase threshold, subject to the source's applicable self-certification and approval provisions.
requirements.quote: The recipient may set for itself a lower or higher micro-purchase threshold.

requirements.statement: A recipient may self-certify a micro-purchase threshold up to and including $50,000. This permission alone does not establish completion of supporting documentation or effectiveness of a proposed threshold.
requirements.quote: Pursuant to 2 CFR 200.320(a)(1), the recipient may self-certify a micro-purchase threshold up to $50,000.

requirements.statement: The self-certification paragraph contains an annual-basis clause, but the supplied sentence omits the action after 'must'. Preserve that drafting limitation rather than inventing a particular annual filing or submission requirement.
requirements.quote: The recipient must on an annual basis and must maintain documentation to be made available to FTA and auditors in accordance with 2 CFR 200.334.

requirements.statement: Maintain self-certification documentation to be made available to FTA and auditors in accordance with 2 CFR 200.334.
requirements.quote: must maintain documentation to be made available to FTA and auditors in accordance with 2 CFR 200.334.

requirements.statement: Include a justification in the micro-purchase threshold self-certification.
requirements.quote: The self-certification must include a justification, clear identification of the threshold, and supporting documentation

requirements.statement: Clearly identify the threshold in the micro-purchase threshold self-certification.
requirements.quote: The self-certification must include a justification, clear identification of the threshold, and supporting documentation

requirements.statement: Support self-certification with documentation of at least one stated alternative: qualification as a low-risk auditee under 2 CFR 200.520 for the most recent audit; an annual internal institutional assessment identifying, mitigating, and managing financial risks; or, for a public institution, consistency of a higher threshold with State law.
requirements.quote: supporting documentation of any of the following: a qualification as a low-risk auditee, in accordance with the criteria in 2 CFR 200.520 for the most recent audit; an annual internal institutional risk assessment to identify, mitigate, and manage financial risks; or, for public institutions, a higher threshold is consistent with State law.

requirements.statement: Obtain approval from the recipient's cognizant agency for indirect costs for a proposed micro-purchase threshold greater than $50,000. Exactly $50,000 does not meet this particular approval trigger.
requirements.quote: A micro-purchase threshold higher than $50,000 must be approved by the recipient’s cognizant agency for indirect costs.

requirements.statement: The source recommends equitable distribution of micro-purchases among qualified suppliers to the extent practicable. This is non-binding guidance, not an additional Boolean authorization condition.
requirements.quote: Under 2 CFR 200.320(a)(1), to the extent practicable, the recipient should distribute micro-purchases equitably among qualified suppliers.

requirements.statement: Do not divide or reduce a procurement merely to come within the micro-purchase limit.
requirements.quote: The recipient may not divide or reduce the size of its procurement merely to come within the micro-purchase limit.

requirements.statement: For micro-purchases, the recipient need not justify the procurement method used. This specific exception qualifies the general procurement-history documentation requirement.
requirements.quote: The recipient need not justify the procurement method used, selection of contract type, or reasons for contractor selection or rejection.

requirements.statement: For micro-purchases, the recipient need not justify selection of contract type. This does not remove the price-reasonableness documentation obligation.
requirements.quote: The recipient need not justify the procurement method used, selection of contract type, or reasons for contractor selection or rejection.

requirements.statement: For micro-purchases, the recipient need not justify reasons for contractor selection or rejection. This does not remove the price-reasonableness documentation obligation.
requirements.quote: The recipient need not justify the procurement method used, selection of contract type, or reasons for contractor selection or rejection.

requirements.statement: The simplified-acquisition amount band requires the aggregate transaction amount to exceed the effective micro-purchase threshold and be at or below the effective simplified acquisition threshold. This is an amount-band condition, not full authorization.
requirements.quote: 2 CFR 200.320(a)(2) authorizes simplified acquisition procedures when the aggregate dollar amount of the procurement transaction is higher than the micro-purchase threshold but does not exceed the simplified acquisition threshold as defined in 2 CFR 200.1; 48 CFR 2.101.

requirements.statement: A recipient may establish a lower threshold for simplified acquisition procedures.
requirements.quote: The recipient may set a lower threshold for simplified acquisition procedures.

requirements.statement: Unlike the micro-purchase threshold, the recipient's simplified acquisition threshold may not exceed the Federal simplified acquisition threshold.
requirements.quote: 2 CFR 200.320 does not permit a recipient to set a simplified acquisition threshold higher than the Federal threshold.

requirements.statement: When using simplified acquisition procedures, obtain price or rate quotations from an adequate number of qualified sources.
requirements.quote: The recipient must obtain price or rate quotations from an adequate number of qualified sources.

requirements.statement: The recipient may exercise judgment in determining an adequate number of sources for simplified acquisition quotations; the supplied provision does not prescribe a fixed number.
requirements.quote: The recipient may exercise judgment in determining what number is adequate.

requirements.statement: Do not divide or reduce a procurement to avoid additional procurement requirements applicable to larger acquisitions.
requirements.quote: The recipient may not divide or reduce the size of its procurement to avoid the additional procurement requirements applicable to larger acquisitions.

requirements.statement: For simplified acquisitions, maintain records supporting the decision to use the simplified acquisition procedure.
requirements.quote: The recipient must maintain records to support its decision to use the simplified acquisition procedure, the selection of contract type, the sources solicited, and the reasons for contractor selection or rejection.

requirements.statement: For simplified acquisitions, maintain records supporting selection of contract type.
requirements.quote: The recipient must maintain records to support its decision to use the simplified acquisition procedure, the selection of contract type, the sources solicited, and the reasons for contractor selection or rejection.

requirements.statement: For simplified acquisitions, maintain records identifying the sources solicited.
requirements.quote: The recipient must maintain records to support its decision to use the simplified acquisition procedure, the selection of contract type, the sources solicited, and the reasons for contractor selection or rejection.

requirements.statement: For simplified acquisitions, maintain records supporting reasons for contractor selection or rejection.
requirements.quote: The recipient must maintain records to support its decision to use the simplified acquisition procedure, the selection of contract type, the sources solicited, and the reasons for contractor selection or rejection.

requirements.statement: Breaking out procurements can support business participation and is not categorically prohibited. The anti-avoidance determination depends on the stated division or reduction and its purpose; a false result does not certify all other splitting as lawful.
requirements.quote: In other circumstances, breaking out procurements may provide greater opportunities for Disadvantaged Business Enterprises (DBEs), small and minority firms, women owned small business enterprises, veteran-owned businesses and businesses committed to environmental sustainability to participate.

process.quote: If permitted by State and local law, the recipient may acquire property and services valued at or below the current micro-purchase threshold without obtaining competitive quotations if the recipient considers the price reasonable based on research, experience, purchase history, or other information, and maintains documents to support its conclusion.

process.action: Determine micro-purchase permission using the ordered output rules: the scoped artificial-split prohibition defeats this route; otherwise allow the route only when the amount ceiling, State/local-law permission, reasonable-price conclusion, and supporting documentation are all satisfied. requirements.statement: This guide edition (Version 2) governs FEMA awards made or disasters declared on or after October 1, 2024. Implementation choice: the decision rules assume the case falls within this edition's date scope, because no date input is declared.
requirements.quote: This document applies to all FEMA awards made or disasters declared on or after October 1, 2024

requirements.statement: Awards made or disasters declared from November 12, 2020 through September 30, 2024 are governed by the June 2021 guide, not this edition.
requirements.quote: For FEMA awards made or disasters declared between November 12, 2020, through September 30, 2024, please refer to the Contract Provisions Guide dated June 2021

requirements.statement: Recipient and subrecipient contracts must contain the applicable provisions described in 2 C.F.R. Part 200 Appendix II.
requirements.quote: contracts must contain the applicable provisions described in Appendix II of this part

requirements.statement: Many provisions apply only when certain circumstances are present, such as the type of work, the dollar amount, or the procurement date.
requirements.quote: Many of the provisions described in this document only apply when certain circumstances are present, such as the type of work being procured, the dollar amount, or the date when it is procured.

requirements.statement: The recipient or subrecipient is solely responsible for ensuring that contract language meets 2 C.F.R. Part 200.
requirements.quote: The recipient or subrecipient is solely responsible for ensuring that all language included in its contracts meets the requirements of 2 C.F.R. Part 200

requirements.statement: The guide does not cover provisions required by state, tribal, or local law. The outputs therefore express no opinion on state-law duties.
requirements.quote: Contract provisions required by applicable state, tribal, or local laws or rules separate from the federal procurement standards.

requirements.statement: Contracts must address termination for cause and for convenience by the recipient or subrecipient. This includes the manner of termination and the basis for settlement.
requirements.quote: Contracts must address termination for cause and for convenience by the recipient or subrecipient, including the manner by which it will be carried out and the basis for settlement.

requirements.statement: The termination provision is required for contracts and purchase orders exceeding $10,000.
requirements.quote: This contract provision is required for contracts and purchase orders exceeding $10,000.

requirements.statement: For contracts at or below $10,000, FEMA suggests a termination for cause provision, but it is not required.
requirements.quote: For contracts at or below $10,000, FEMA suggests including a termination for cause provision, but this is not required.

requirements.statement: FEMA recommends (does not require) that termination clauses be actionable and specific.
requirements.quote: FEMA recommends that termination clauses be actionable and specific.

requirements.statement: When required by the federal program legislation, all prime construction contracts over $2,000 must include a Davis-Bacon Act compliance provision.
requirements.quote: When required by the federal program legislation, all prime construction contracts over $2,000 awarded by recipients or subrecipients must include a provision for compliance with the Davis-Bacon Act.

requirements.statement: The Davis-Bacon Act does not apply to all FEMA financial assistance programs. Applicability must be determined from the NOFO, program guidance, or the FEMA grant representative.
requirements.quote: Recipients and subrecipients should refer to applicable NOFO or other program guidance or contact their applicable FEMA grant representative to determine if this provision is required for the procurement.

requirements.statement: Exception with precedence: the Davis-Bacon clause is not federally required for procurements under PA or HMA programs.
requirements.quote: However, the Davis-Bacon Act clause is not federally required for procurements under FEMA’s Public Assistance (PA) or Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) Programs.

requirements.statement: If Davis-Bacon applies, the recipient or subrecipient must place the current Department of Labor prevailing wage determination in each solicitation.
requirements.quote: The recipient or subrecipient must place a copy of the Department of Labor’s current prevailing wage determination in each solicitation.

requirements.statement: If Davis-Bacon applies, contracts or subcontracts must be awarded on condition that the prevailing wage determination is accepted.
requirements.quote: Contracts or subcontracts must be awarded on the condition that the prevailing wage determination is accepted.

requirements.statement: If Davis-Bacon applies, the recipient or subrecipient must report all suspected or reported violations to the federal agency.
requirements.quote: The recipient or subrecipient must report all suspected or reported violations to the federal agency.

requirements.statement: Contracts subject to Davis-Bacon must also include a Copeland Anti-Kickback Act compliance provision.
requirements.quote: Contracts subject to the Davis-Bacon Act, must also include a provision for compliance with the Copeland

requirements.statement: If applicable, the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) must be included in full in all applicable contracts.
requirements.quote: the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) in full into all applicable contracts

requirements.statement: The Copeland provision applies to prime construction contracts above $2,000 when Davis-Bacon also applies.
requirements.quote: For all prime construction contracts above $2,000, when the Davis-Bacon Act also applies

requirements.statement: Where applicable, contracts must include a provision for compliance with statutory work hours and safety standards.
requirements.quote: contracts must include a provision for compliance with statutory requirements on work hours and safety standards.

requirements.statement: Each contractor must base wages for every mechanic and laborer on a standard 40-hour work week.
requirements.quote: each contractor must base wages for every mechanic and laborer on a standard 40-hour work week.

requirements.statement: The work-hours provision applies to procurements over $100,000 that involve employment of mechanics, laborers, and construction work.
requirements.quote: This required contract provision applies to all procurements over $100,000 that involve the employment of mechanics, laborers, and construction work.

requirements.statement: Exception with precedence: the requirements do not apply to purchases of open-market supplies, materials, or articles, or to contracts for transportation or transmission of intelligence.
requirements.quote: These requirements do not apply to the purchase of supplies, materials, or articles ordinarily available on the open market, contracts for transportation or transmission of intelligence.

requirements.statement: If applicable, the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5) must be included verbatim in all applicable contracts and in full in subcontracts.
requirements.quote: the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5), verbatim, into all applicable contracts

requirements.statement: For contracts subject only to CWHSSA and not to other statutes cited in 29 C.F.R. § 5.1, a clause meeting 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(c) must also be inserted. Specific language is not required.
requirements.quote: the recipient or subrecipient must also insert a clause meeting the requirements of 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(c).

requirements.statement: Contracts must contain a provision requiring contractors to comply with the Clean Air Act and the Federal Water Pollution Control Act.
requirements.quote: Contracts must contain a provision requiring contractors to comply with the Clean Air Act

requirements.statement: Violations must be reported to FEMA and to the EPA Regional Office.
requirements.quote: Violations must be reported to FEMA and the Regional Office of the Environmental Protection Agency.

requirements.statement: The Clean Air/Water provision is required for all procurements over $150,000.
requirements.quote: This contract provision is required for all procurements over $150,000.

requirements.statement: The suggested sample language has the contractor flow the requirements down to subcontracts exceeding $150,000. This is suggested language, not mandated text.
requirements.quote: The contractor agrees to include these requirements in each subcontract exceeding $150,000

requirements.statement: Definition of construction work (41 C.F.R. § 60-1.3), as reproduced in the guide.
requirements.quote: construction, rehabilitation, alteration, conversion, extension, demolition or repair of buildings, highways, or other changes or improvements to real property

process.action: Confirm that the award or disaster declaration date falls within this edition's scope (on or after October 1, 2024). Otherwise, refer to the prior guide.
process.quote: This document applies to all FEMA awards made or disasters declared on or after October 1, 2024

process.action: Collect the case facts that drive applicability: contract amount, work type or category, FEMA program, program-legislation Davis-Bacon applicability, and employment of mechanics or laborers.

process.action: Termination: require the provision if the contract or purchase order exceeds $10,000. At or below $10,000 it is suggested only, not required.
process.quote: This contract provision is required for contracts and purchase orders exceeding $10,000.

process.action: If termination is required, draft it to address cause and convenience, the manner of termination, and the basis for settlement. FEMA recommends (but does not require) that the clause be actionable and specific.
process.quote: Contracts must address termination for cause and for convenience by the recipient or subrecipient, including the manner by which it will be carried out and the basis for settlement.

process.action: Davis-Bacon: first apply the PA/HMA exclusion, under which the clause is not federally required.
process.quote: However, the Davis-Bacon Act clause is not federally required for procurements under FEMA’s Public Assistance (PA) or Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) Programs.

process.action: For other programs, check whether the contract is a prime construction contract over $2,000 and whether the federal program legislation requires Davis-Bacon. Where legislation applicability is unknown, consult the NOFO, program guidance, or the FEMA grant representative.
process.quote: When required by the federal program legislation, all prime construction contracts over $2,000 awarded by recipients or subrecipients must include a provision for compliance with the Davis-Bacon Act.

process.action: If Davis-Bacon applies: place the wage determination in the solicitation, award conditioned on acceptance, include 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) in full, address Copeland compliance, and report violations.
process.quote: Contracts or subcontracts must be awarded on the condition that the prevailing wage determination is accepted.

process.action: Work hours: first apply the exclusions for open-market supplies, transportation, and transmission of intelligence.
process.quote: These requirements do not apply to the purchase of supplies, materials, or articles ordinarily available on the open market, contracts for transportation or transmission of intelligence.

process.action: For non-excluded procurements, check for amount over $100,000, employment of mechanics or laborers, and construction work. Keep the result unknown where the work type cannot be classified.
process.quote: This required contract provision applies to all procurements over $100,000 that involve the employment of mechanics, laborers, and construction work.

process.action: If work hours applies: include 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5) verbatim and flow it down. Add a 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(c) clause where the contract is subject only to CWHSSA.
process.quote: the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5), verbatim, into all applicable contracts

process.action: Clean Air/Water: require the provision for procurements over $150,000.
process.quote: This contract provision is required for all procurements over $150,000.

process.action: If Clean Air/Water applies: include the compliance provision and provide for reporting violations to FEMA and the EPA Regional Office.
process.quote: Violations must be reported to FEMA and the Regional Office of the Environmental Protection Agency.

process.action: Final review: the recipient or subrecipient confirms that all contract language meets 2 C.F.R. Part 200. This draft is unapproved and is not a legal determination.

requirements.statement: The supplied edition applies to FEMA awards made or disasters declared on or after October 1, 2024. This blueprint interprets that fixed edition and does not determine award-date eligibility from the supplied inputs.
requirements.quote: This document applies to all FEMA awards made or disasters declared on or after October 1, 2024

requirements.statement: A contract is the instrument used to purchase property or services needed to carry out a project or program under a federal award; it is not the federal award or subaward itself.
requirements.quote: A contract, for the purposes of this Guide, does not mean a federal award or subaward.

requirements.statement: Contracts must contain the applicable Appendix II provisions.
requirements.quote: recipient’s or subrecipient’s contracts must contain the applicable provisions described in Appendix II of this part

requirements.statement: The recipient or subrecipient remains responsible for ensuring that included contract language satisfies the applicable requirements; this blueprint does not approve contract language.
requirements.quote: The recipient or subrecipient is solely responsible for ensuring that all language included in its contracts meets the requirements of 2 C.F.R. Part 200, including 2 C.F.R. § 200.327 and Appendix II.

requirements.statement: Include the section 2 termination provision in contracts and purchase orders exceeding $10,000.
requirements.quote: This contract provision is required for contracts and purchase orders exceeding $10,000.

requirements.statement: At or below $10,000, the section 2.1 termination provision is not required. This is non-requirement, not a prohibition on including a provision.
requirements.quote: For contracts at or below $10,000, FEMA suggests including a termination for cause provision, but this is not required.

requirements.statement: FEMA suggests a termination-for-cause provision at or below $10,000; that suggestion is not a mandatory cause-and-convenience provision.
requirements.quote: For contracts at or below $10,000, FEMA suggests including a termination for cause provision, but this is not required.

requirements.statement: When required, the termination provision must address termination for cause and convenience by the recipient or subrecipient, the manner of termination, and the basis for settlement.
requirements.quote: Contracts must address termination for cause and for convenience by the recipient or subrecipient, including the manner by which it will be carried out and the basis for settlement.

requirements.statement: FEMA recommends actionable and specific termination clauses; this recommendation does not change the section 2.1 amount threshold.
requirements.quote: FEMA recommends that termination clauses be actionable and specific.

requirements.statement: When required by federal program legislation, include a Davis-Bacon compliance provision in prime construction contracts over $2,000.
requirements.quote: When required by the federal program legislation, all prime construction contracts over $2,000 awarded by recipients or subrecipients must include a provision for compliance with the Davis-Bacon Act.

requirements.statement: The Davis-Bacon clause is not federally required for procurements under PA or HMA. This exclusion controls the scoped federal-requirement decision even if the supplied program-legislation field says yes.
requirements.quote: However, the Davis-Bacon Act clause is not federally required for procurements under FEMA’s Public Assistance (PA) or Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) Programs.

requirements.statement: For programs not resolved by the express exclusion, the guide directs recipients and subrecipients to program guidance or their FEMA grant representative to determine applicability. Unknown program-legislation applicability is not an affirmative finding of applicability.
requirements.quote: Recipients and subrecipients should refer to applicable NOFO or other program guidance or contact their applicable FEMA grant representative to determine if this provision is required for the procurement.

requirements.statement: If Davis-Bacon applies, place the Department of Labor's current prevailing wage determination in each solicitation.
requirements.quote: The recipient or subrecipient must place a copy of the Department of Labor’s current prevailing wage determination in each solicitation.

requirements.statement: If Davis-Bacon applies, award contracts or subcontracts on the condition that the prevailing wage determination is accepted.
requirements.quote: Contracts or subcontracts must be awarded on the condition that the prevailing wage determination is accepted.

requirements.statement: If Davis-Bacon applies, report all suspected or reported violations to the federal agency.
requirements.quote: The recipient or subrecipient must report all suspected or reported violations to the federal agency.

requirements.statement: Contracts subject to Davis-Bacon must also include compliance with the Copeland Anti-Kickback Act; the guide explains that this is incorporated into the required Davis-Bacon provision, so a separate provision is unnecessary.
requirements.quote: Contracts subject to the Davis-Bacon Act, must also include a provision for compliance with the Copeland “Anti-Kickback” Act.

requirements.statement: A separate Copeland Anti-Kickback provision may be included even though the required Davis-Bacon provision incorporates its regulatory requirements.
requirements.quote: However, the recipient or subrecipient may include a separate contract provision specific to the Copeland “Anti-Kickback” Act.

requirements.statement: If Davis-Bacon applies, include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) in full in applicable contracts.
requirements.quote: If applicable per the standard described above, the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) in full into all applicable contracts, and all applicable contractors must include these provisions in full in any subcontracts.

requirements.statement: Section 4.3 requires applicable contractors to include the Davis-Bacon provisions in full in subcontracts. For drafting under this guide, follow this express full-text requirement rather than treating section 4.2's general incorporation-by-reference description as sufficient.
requirements.quote: If applicable per the standard described above, the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) in full into all applicable contracts, and all applicable contractors must include these provisions in full in any subcontracts.

requirements.statement: Section 4.2 describes inserting or incorporating the Davis-Bacon clauses by reference into subcontracts; section 4.3 separately specifies full inclusion. Preserve that distinction when preparing the contract.
requirements.quote: the recipient’s or subrecipient’s contractor and any subcontractors are required to insert, or incorporate by reference, the clauses contained at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11)

requirements.statement: Section 6.1 requires the work-hours/safety provision for procurements over $100,000 involving the described employment and construction work. Prime construction with mechanics or laborers is expressly covered unless an express exclusion applies.
requirements.quote: This required contract provision applies to all procurements over $100,000 that involve the employment of mechanics, laborers, and construction work.

requirements.statement: Purchases of supplies, materials, or articles ordinarily available on the open market are excluded from section 6.1.
requirements.quote: These requirements do not apply to the purchase of supplies, materials, or articles ordinarily available on the open market, contracts for transportation or transmission of intelligence.

requirements.statement: Contracts for transportation are excluded from section 6.1.
requirements.quote: These requirements do not apply to the purchase of supplies, materials, or articles ordinarily available on the open market, contracts for transportation or transmission of intelligence.

requirements.statement: Contracts for transmission of intelligence are excluded from section 6.1.
requirements.quote: These requirements do not apply to the purchase of supplies, materials, or articles ordinarily available on the open market, contracts for transportation or transmission of intelligence.

requirements.statement: If section 6 applies, include 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5) verbatim in applicable contracts.
requirements.quote: If applicable per the standard described above, the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5), verbatim, into all applicable contracts, and all applicable contractors must include these provisions, in full, into any subcontracts.

requirements.statement: If section 6 applies, include its required provisions in full in subcontracts.
requirements.quote: all applicable contractors must include these provisions, in full, into any subcontracts.

requirements.statement: For a contract subject only to the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act and not to any other statutes cited in 29 C.F.R. § 5.1, additionally insert a clause meeting 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(c).
requirements.quote: In addition to the required language from 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5), in any contract subject only to the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act and not to any other statutes cited in 29 C.F.R. § 5.1, the recipient or subrecipient must also insert a clause meeting the requirements of 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(c).

requirements.statement: The additional section 6.2 clause has no mandated specific wording in the guide; FEMA supplies suggested wording. This does not relax the separate verbatim requirement for § 5.5(b)(1)-(5).
requirements.quote: Specific language is not required, but FEMA has provided suggested language below.

requirements.statement: Include the section 8 Clean Air/Water provision for all procurements over $150,000. The scoped amount condition is not met at exactly $150,000.
requirements.quote: This contract provision is required for all procurements over $150,000.

requirements.statement: When section 8 applies, the contract provision must require contractor compliance with both the Clean Air Act and the Federal Water Pollution Control Act.
requirements.quote: Contracts must contain a provision requiring contractors to comply with the Clean Air Act

requirements.statement: For the applicable Clean Air/Water requirements, violations must be reported to FEMA and the EPA Regional Office.
requirements.quote: Violations must be reported to FEMA and the Regional Office of the Environmental Protection Agency.

process.action: For cases not excluded by P04, evaluate the over-$2,000 amount condition, prime-construction classification, and program-legislation requirement. process.quote: If applicable per the standard described above, the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(1)-(11) in full into all applicable contracts, and all applicable contractors must include these provisions in full in any subcontracts.

process.quote: These requirements do not apply to the purchase of supplies, materials, or articles ordinarily available on the open market, contracts for transportation or transmission of intelligence.

process.action: For work not excluded by P08, resolve false at or below $100,000 or when mechanics/laborers are not involved. process.quote: This required contract provision applies to all procurements over $100,000 that involve the employment of mechanics, laborers, and construction work.

process.action: If the work-hours/safety provision is required, include § 5.5(b)(1)-(5) verbatim in applicable contracts and in full in applicable subcontracts. The guide's suggested additional wording does not replace this required language.
process.quote: If applicable per the standard described above, the recipient or subrecipient must include the provisions at 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(b)(1)-(5), verbatim, into all applicable contracts, and all applicable contractors must include these provisions, in full, into any subcontracts.

process.quote: This contract provision is required for all procurements over $150,000.

requirements.statement: A proposal modification is a change made before the solicitation closing date and time, in response to an amendment, or to correct a mistake at any time before award. The supplied item_kind is authoritative for this interface; the blueprint does not reclassify it.
requirements.quote: Proposal modification is a change made to a proposal before the solicitation closing date and time, or made in response to an amendment, or made to correct a mistake at any time before award.

requirements.statement: A proposal revision is a change made after the solicitation closing date, at the request of or as allowed by a contracting officer, as the result of negotiations. The supplied item_kind is authoritative for this interface.
requirements.quote: Proposal revision is a change to a proposal made after the solicitation closing date, at the request of or as allowed by a contracting officer, as the result of negotiations.

requirements.statement: Upon receipt at the solicitation's specified location, mark proposals and RFI information with the date and time of receipt.
requirements.quote: Upon receipt at the location specified in the solicitation, proposals and information received in response to a request for information (RFI) shall be marked with the date and time of receipt and shall be transmitted to the designated officials.

requirements.statement: Transmit proposals and RFI information received at the specified location to the designated officials.
requirements.quote: shall be transmitted to the designated officials.

requirements.statement: Submit proposals, revisions, and modifications so that they reach the designated Government office by the specified solicitation time.
requirements.quote: Offerors are responsible for submitting proposals, and any revisions, and modifications, so as to reach the Government office designated in the solicitation by the time specified in the solicitation.

requirements.statement: Use any transmission method authorized by the solicitation.
requirements.quote: Offerors may use any transmission method authorized by the solicitation (i.e., regular mail, electronic commerce, or facsimile).

requirements.statement: If the solicitation specifies no receipt time, the receipt deadline is 4:30 p.m., local time at the designated Government office, on the proposal due date. This is upstream deadline context, not an additional test overriding received_late.
requirements.quote: If no time is specified in the solicitation, the time for receipt is 4:30 p.m., local time, for the designated Government office on the date that proposals are due.

requirements.statement: A proposal, modification, or revision received at the designated Government office after the exact specified receipt time is late. For the requested decisions, received_late supplies this fact using the effective deadline.
requirements.quote: Any proposal, modification, or revision, that is received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is "late"

requirements.statement: Subject to the overriding successful-proposal modification rule in 15.208(b)(2), do not consider a late item unless it was received before award, the contracting officer determines that accepting it would not unduly delay the acquisition, and at least one alternative in 15.208(b)(1)(i) through (iii) applies.
requirements.quote: Any proposal, modification, or revision, that is received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is "late" and will not be considered unless it is received before award is made, the contracting officer determines that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition; and-

requirements.statement: The ordinary late-item exception in 15.208(b)(1) requires receipt before award. This gate does not restrict the separate 15.208(b)(2) rule.
requirements.quote: will not be considered unless it is received before award is made

requirements.statement: The ordinary late-item exception in 15.208(b)(1) requires a contracting-officer determination that accepting the item would not unduly delay the acquisition. This gate does not restrict the separate 15.208(b)(2) rule.
requirements.quote: the contracting officer determines that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition

requirements.statement: One alternative under 15.208(b)(1) is authorized electronic transmission received at the initial Government infrastructure entry point no later than 5:00 p.m. one working day before the specified proposal receipt date. An earlier working day also satisfies this cutoff, regardless of its minute of receipt.
requirements.quote: If it was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the solicitation, it was received at the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure not later than 5:00 p.m. one working day prior to the date specified for receipt of proposals

requirements.statement: Another alternative under 15.208(b)(1) requires acceptable evidence establishing both receipt at the Government installation designated for proposal receipt and Government control before the receipt deadline.
requirements.quote: There is acceptable evidence to establish that it was received at the Government installation designated for receipt of proposals and was under the Government’s control prior to the time set for receipt of proposals

requirements.statement: Being the only proposal received is the third alternative under 15.208(b)(1). Use the supplied only_proposal_received fact directly without adding another item_kind restriction.
requirements.quote: It was the only proposal received.

requirements.statement: Consider a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal that makes its terms more favorable to the Government at any time it is received. This overrides the ordinary before-award, no-undue-delay, and alternative-route gates.
requirements.quote: However, a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted.

requirements.statement: A qualifying late modification under 15.208(b)(2) may be accepted. Acceptance is permissive and is not decided by late_submission_considerable.
requirements.quote: However, a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted.

requirements.statement: Acceptable installation receipt-time evidence includes the installation's time/date stamp on the wrapper, other installation-maintained documentary receipt evidence, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel. Do not impose a documentary-only evidence requirement.
requirements.quote: Acceptable evidence to establish the time of receipt at the Government installation includes the time/date stamp of that installation on the proposal wrapper, other documentary evidence of receipt maintained by the installation, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.

requirements.statement: The deemed deadline extension triggers when an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes, that interruption prevents timely proposal receipt at the designated office, and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the closing date.
requirements.quote: If an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes so that proposals cannot be received at the Government office designated for receipt of proposals by the exact time specified in the solicitation, and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the solicitation closing date

requirements.statement: When 15.208(d) triggers, the deemed deadline is the same specified time of day on the first workday on which normal Government processes resume. No calendar date can be calculated from the declared inputs.
requirements.quote: the time specified for receipt of proposals will be deemed to be extended to the same time of day specified in the solicitation on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume.

requirements.statement: Promptly notify the offeror when its proposal, modification, or revision was received late, unless the conjunctive exception in 15.208(f) applies. Considerability does not itself remove this notice duty.
requirements.quote: The contracting officer must promptly notify any offeror if its proposal, modification, or revision was received late

requirements.statement: The required late-receipt notice must inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered.
requirements.quote: must inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered

requirements.statement: The 15.208(f) prompt late-receipt notice exception requires both imminent contract award and sufficiency of the notice prescribed in 15.503(b). Use award_notice_would_suffice as the supplied procedural fact; do not infer it from imminence alone.
requirements.quote: unless contract award is imminent and the notice prescribed in 15.503(b) would suffice.

requirements.statement: Hold late proposals and modifications that are not considered unopened until after award, subject to opening for identification. This paragraph's custody obligation is not expanded to revisions merely because other paragraphs mention revisions.
requirements.quote: Late proposals and modifications that are not considered must be held unopened, unless opened for identification, until after award and then retained with other unsuccessful proposals.

requirements.statement: The unopened-custody requirement permits opening an unconsidered late proposal or modification for identification.
requirements.quote: must be held unopened, unless opened for identification, until after award

requirements.statement: After award, retain unconsidered late proposals and modifications with the other unsuccessful proposals.
requirements.quote: until after award and then retained with other unsuccessful proposals.

requirements.statement: For each late proposal, modification, revision, or withdrawal, include the date and hour of receipt in the contracting office files if available. Withdrawals are outside the declared item_kind interface.
requirements.quote: If available, the following must be included in the contracting office files for each late proposal, modification, revision, or withdrawal: (1) The date and hour of receipt.

requirements.statement: For each late proposal, modification, revision, or withdrawal, include a statement of whether the proposal was considered for award and supporting rationale in the contracting office files if available.
requirements.quote: A statement regarding whether the proposal was considered for award, with supporting rationale.

requirements.statement: For each late proposal, modification, revision, or withdrawal, include the envelope, wrapper, or other receipt-date evidence in the contracting office files if available.
requirements.quote: The envelope, wrapper, or other evidence of date of receipt.

However, a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted.

Any proposal, modification, or revision, that is received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is "late" and will not be considered unless it is received before award is made, the contracting officer determines that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition; and- (i) If it was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the solicitation, it was received at the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure not later than 5:00 p.m. one working day prior to the date specified for receipt of proposals; or (ii) There is acceptable evidence to establish that it was received at the Government installation designated for receipt of proposals and was under the Government’s control prior to the time set for receipt of proposals; or (iii) It was the only proposal received.

The contracting officer must promptly notify any offeror if its proposal, modification, or revision was received late, and must inform the offeror whether its proposal will be considered, unless contract award is imminent and the notice prescribed in 15.503(b) would suffice.

advisory_review.scope: The first-repetition OpenAI and Anthropic FEMA outputs in the recorded corrected-analysis snapshot; no claims about later repetitions or every other output.

affected_contract_field.description: Procurement category. construction means prime construction; other may contain uncharacterised work.

finding.source_quote: When required by the federal program legislation, all prime construction contracts over $2,000 awarded by recipients or subrecipients must include a provision for compliance with the Davis-Bacon Act.
finding.source_requirement: Contract classification and program-legislation applicability matter. The source also tells recipients to consult program guidance to determine applicability and expressly excludes PA/HMA.
finding.key_assumption: The key sets false whenever contract_category is not prime_construction, including other. This treats other as a positive assertion of known non-prime-construction status.
finding.alternative_input_reading: The input description says other may contain uncharacterised work. A category not yet established does not establish that it is nonconstruction. Program-legislation applicability is also unknown in the three affected cases.
finding.observed_models: OpenAI reaches default unknown; Anthropic reaches its explicit program-legislation unknown branch. Neither converts the supplied uncertain applicability into a mandatory clause.
finding.advisory_conclusion: The six disagreements expose one ambiguity in the authored input ontology/key. Unknown is defensible under the unclassified-work reading. False is defensible only if the enum values are intended as exhaustive mutually exclusive classifications with other guaranteeing nonconstruction, a guarantee the field description does not clearly provide. The observed differences do not establish six model errors.
finding.evaluator_assessment: The inspected first-matching-rule traces match the generated JSON conditions. No DSL interpreter defect was identified for these six decisions; this does not audit every evaluator path.
finding.current_reporting: Retain all frozen expected values and six recorded disagreements. Add this advisory note beside the descriptive draft-key agreement. Do not change the denominator, add accepted labels or assign an accuracy penalty/credit after observing outputs.
finding.future_revision: Before a separately identified future campaign, distinguish known_nonconstruction from unclassified (or provide a tri-state is_prime_construction field). Keep applicability facts separate from source knowledge, freeze the mapping, and add explicit paired cases for classification known/unknown and legislation yes/no/unknown.
